translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 287

sentences.zh: 【後漢紀二】 起強圉協洽五月，盡著雍涒灘二月，不滿一年。

translations.literal: [Later Han Records 2] Beginning in the fifth month of the year Qiangyu Xieqia, ending in the second month of the year Zhuoyong Tantan—not a full year.
translations.idiomatic: [Later Han Records 2] From Qiangyu Xieqia (fifth month) through Zhuoyong Tantan (second month)—less than one year in all.

sentences.zh: 高祖睿文聖武昭肅孝皇帝中天福十二年（

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Tianfu of the Gaozu Emperor—styled Ruiwen Shengwu Zhaosu Xiaohuangdi—(
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Tianfu of Emperor Gaozu, posthumously styled Ruiwen Shengwu Zhaosu Xiaohuangdi (

sentences.zh: 丁未，公元九四七年）

translations.literal: dingwei, corresponding to the year 947 CE)
translations.idiomatic: dingwei, corresponding to 947 CE)

sentences.zh: 五月，乙酉塑，永康王兀欲召延壽及張礪、和凝、李崧、馮道於所館飲酒。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on yiyou the first day of the month, Prince Yongkang Wang Wuyu summoned Yanshou together with Zhang Li, He Ning, Li Song, and Feng Dao to drink wine at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the first day of the month (yiyou), Prince Yongkang Wang Yelü Ruan summoned Feng Yanshou, Zhang Li, He Ning, Li Song, and Feng Dao to drink at his lodge.

sentences.zh: 兀欲妻素以兄事延壽，兀欲從容謂延壽曰：「妹自上國來，寧欲見之乎？」

translations.literal: Wuyu's wife had always treated Yanshou as an elder brother. Wuyu said calmly to Yanshou, "My younger sister has come from the Upper Kingdom—would you perhaps like to see her?"
translations.idiomatic: Ruan's wife had long addressed Yanshou as an elder brother. Ruan said casually to him, "My sister has arrived from the north—would you care to see her?"

sentences.zh: 延壽欣然與之俱入。

translations.literal: Yanshou gladly went in with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou gladly went inside with him.

sentences.zh: 良久，兀欲出，謂礪等曰：「燕王謀反，適已鎖之矣。」

translations.literal: After a long while Wuyu came out and said to Li and the others, "The Prince of Yan plotted rebellion; I have just now put him in chains."
translations.idiomatic: After some time Ruan came out and told Li and the rest, "The Prince of Yan was plotting rebellion—I have just had him locked up."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「先帝在汴時，遺我一籌，許我知南朝軍國。

translations.literal: He added, "When the late emperor was at Bian, he left me one tally and permitted me to know the military and civil affairs of the Southern Court.
translations.idiomatic: He went on, "When the late emperor was at Bian, he left me one tally and allowed me to oversee the Southern Court's military and civil affairs.

sentences.zh: 近者臨崩，別無遺詔。

translations.literal: Recently, on the verge of death, there was no other testamentary edict.
translations.idiomatic: As he lay dying recently, he issued no other testamentary edict.

sentences.zh: 而燕王擅自知南朝軍國，豈理邪！」

translations.literal: Yet the Prince of Yan on his own authority knew the military and civil affairs of the Southern Court—how can that be right!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Prince of Yan took it upon himself to manage those affairs—how can that be justified!"

sentences.zh: 下令：「延壽親黨，皆釋不問。」

translations.literal: He ordered, "All of Yanshou's kin and associates are to be released and not questioned."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered, "All of Yanshou's kin and associates are to be released without inquiry."

sentences.zh: 間一日，兀欲至待賢館受蕃、漢官謁賀，笑謂張礪等曰：「燕王果於此禮上，吾以鐵騎圍之，諸公亦不免矣。」

translations.literal: One day later Wuyu went to the Hall of Awaiting the Worthy to receive the homage and congratulations of Khitan and Han officials, and said with a laugh to Zhang Li and the others, "If the Prince of Yan had indeed come to this ceremony, I would have surrounded him with iron cavalry—you gentlemen would not have escaped either."
translations.idiomatic: The next day Ruan went to the Hall of Awaiting the Worthy to receive homage from Khitan and Han officials. He said with a laugh to Zhang Li and the others, "Had the Prince of Yan actually come to this ceremony, I would have surrounded him with armored cavalry—you would not have escaped either."

sentences.zh: 後數日，集蕃、漢之臣於府署，宣契丹主遺制。

translations.literal: Several days later he assembled Khitan and Han ministers at the government offices and proclaimed the late Khitan ruler's testamentary instructions.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later he gathered Khitan and Han ministers at the government offices and announced the late Khitan emperor's testamentary instructions.

sentences.zh: 其略曰：「永康王，大聖皇帝之嫡孫，人皇王之長子，太后鍾愛，群情允歸，可於中京即皇帝位。」

translations.literal: The gist read: "Prince Yongkang Wang, the legitimate grandson of the Great Sage Emperor and eldest son of the Human Sovereign King, beloved by the empress dowager and with the assent of all hearts, may ascend the imperial throne at the Central Capital."
translations.idiomatic: The gist was: "Prince Yongkang Wang, legitimate grandson of the Great Sage Emperor and eldest son of the Human Sovereign King, beloved by the empress dowager and approved by all, may ascend the throne at the Central Capital."

sentences.zh: 於是始舉哀成服。

translations.literal: Thereupon mourning was first raised and mourning garments donned.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did he begin mourning and put on mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 既而易吉服見群臣，不復行喪，歌吹之聲不絕於內。

translations.literal: Soon after he changed into auspicious garments to see the ministers, no longer observed mourning, and the sounds of song and pipes never ceased within.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he changed into court dress to receive the ministers, abandoned mourning observances, and music and revelry never ceased within the palace.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，以絳州防禦使王晏為建雄節度使。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Defense Commissioner of Jiang Prefecture Wang Yan was made Military Commissioner of Jianxiong.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Jiang Prefecture defense commissioner Wang Yan was appointed military commissioner of Jianxiong.

sentences.zh: 帝集群臣庭議進取，諸將咸請出師井陘，攻取鎮、魏，先定河北，則河南拱手自服。

translations.literal: The emperor assembled the ministers in court to deliberate on advancing. The generals all asked to march out through Jingxing Pass, attack and take Zhen and Wei, first secure Hebei, and then Henan would bow of its own accord.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor convened the ministers in open court to discuss the advance. The generals all urged marching through Jingxing Pass to seize Zhen and Wei, secure Hebei first, and Henan would then submit of its own accord.

sentences.zh: 帝欲自石會趨上黨，郭威曰：「虜主雖死，黨眾猶盛，各據堅城。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to go himself from Shihui toward Shangdang. Guo Wei said, "Although the barbarian ruler is dead, his faction is still strong and each holds a stout walled city.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to advance personally from Shihui toward Shangdang. Guo Wei said, "Though the Khitan ruler is dead, his followers remain strong, each holding a fortified city.

sentences.zh: 我出河北，兵少路迂，傍無應援，若群虜合勢，共擊我軍，進則遮前，退則邀後，糧餉路絕，此危道也。

translations.literal: If we go out through Hebei, our troops are few and the route circuitous, with no support on the flanks. If the barbarians unite their strength and strike our army together, they will block us in front if we advance and cut us off in the rear if we retreat, and our grain and supplies will be cut off—this is a perilous road.
translations.idiomatic: If we march through Hebei, our forces are few and the route long, with no allies nearby. If the Khitan unite and attack us together, they can block us ahead and ambush us behind, cutting off our supplies—that is a deadly route.

sentences.zh: 上黨山路險澀，粟少民殘，無以供億，亦不可由。

translations.literal: The Shangdang road is rugged and difficult, grain is scarce and the people devastated, and there is nothing to supply our needs—it cannot be taken either.
translations.idiomatic: The Shangdang route is steep and treacherous, grain is scarce and the people exhausted—there is nothing to sustain an army. That way is impossible too.

sentences.zh: 近者陝、晉二鎮，相繼款附，引兵從之，萬無一失，不出兩旬，洛、汴定矣。」

translations.literal: Recently the two circuits of Shaan and Jin have submitted in succession. If we lead our troops along that line, there is not one chance in ten thousand of failure; within less than twenty days Luoyang and Bian will be settled."
translations.idiomatic: Shaan and Jin circuits have lately submitted one after another. March along that line and we cannot fail—in less than twenty days Luoyang and Bian will be ours."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿言是也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Your words are correct."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are right."

sentences.zh: 蘇逢吉等曰：「史弘肇大軍已屯上黨，群虜繼遁，不若出天井，抵孟津為便。」

translations.literal: Su Fengji and others said, "Shi Hongzhao's great army is already encamped at Shangdang and the barbarian bands are fleeing in succession; it would be better to go out through Tianjing and reach Mengjin—that would be convenient."
translations.idiomatic: Su Fengji and others said, "Shi Hongzhao's main force is already at Shangdang and the Khitan are retreating in succession. It would be better to march out through Tianjing Pass and reach Mengjin."

sentences.zh: 司天奏：「太歲在午，不利南行。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Astronomy reported, "The Year Star is in the Wu position; travel to the south is unfavorable.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Astronomy reported, "The Year Star stands in wu—travel south is ill-omened.

sentences.zh: 宜由晉、絳抵陝。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to go by Jin and Jiang to reach Shaan."
translations.idiomatic: The army should go by Jin and Jiang to reach Shaan."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，詔以十二日發北京，告諭諸道。

translations.literal: On xinmao, an edict ordered that on the twelfth day the army would set out from the Northern Capital, and the various circuits were notified.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, an edict fixed the twelfth as the day to depart the Northern Capital, and all circuits were notified.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以太原尹崇為北京留守，以趙州刺史李存瑰為副留守，河東幕僚真定李驤為少尹，牙將太原蔚進為馬步指揮使以佐之。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Taiyuan Intendant Chong was made Northern Capital regent; Zhao Prefecture inspector Li Cungui was made deputy regent; Hedong staff member Li Zan of Zhending was made junior intendant; and garrison officer Wei Jin of Taiyuan was made commander of horse and foot to assist them.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Taiyuan intendant Chong was appointed regent of the Northern Capital; Zhao prefecture inspector Li Cungui became deputy regent; Hedong staff officer Li Zan of Zhending became junior intendant; and garrison officer Wei Jin of Taiyuan was made commander of horse and foot to assist them.

sentences.zh: 存瑰，唐莊宗之從弟也。

translations.literal: Cungui was a younger cousin of Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong.
translations.idiomatic: Cungui was a younger cousin of Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang.

sentences.zh: 是日，劉晞棄洛陽，奔大梁。

translations.literal: That day Liu Xi abandoned Luoyang and fled to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Liu Xi abandoned Luoyang and fled to Daliang.

sentences.zh: 武安節度副使、天策府都尉、領鎮南節度使馬希廣，楚文昭王希範之母弟也，性謹順，希範愛之，使判內外諸司事。

translations.literal: Wu'an Military Commissioner deputy, Tiancefu commandant, and concurrent Military Commissioner of Zhennan Ma Xiguang was the younger brother by the same mother of Chu King Wenzhao Xi Fan; his nature was cautious and obedient, Xi Fan loved him, and had him oversee the affairs of all inner and outer offices.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xiguang, deputy military commissioner of Wu'an, commandant of the Tiancefu, and concurrent military commissioner of Zhennan, was a younger brother of Chu King Wenzhao Ma Xifan by the same mother. Gentle and dutiful by nature, Xifan favored him and put him in charge of all internal and external offices.

sentences.zh: 壬辰夜，希範卒，將佐議所立。

translations.literal: On the night of renchen Xi Fan died, and the officers deliberated whom to install.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of renchen Xifan died, and his officers debated whom to enthrone.

sentences.zh: 都指揮所張少敵，都押牙袁友恭，以武平節度使知永州事希萼，於希範諸弟為最長，請立之。

translations.literal: Director of the command headquarters Zhang Shaodi and chief adjutant Yuan Yougong, on the grounds that Military Commissioner of Wuping and Yongzhou administrator Ma Xie was the eldest among Xi Fan's brothers, asked that he be installed.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the command headquarters Zhang Shaodi and chief adjutant Yuan Yougong urged enthroning Ma Xie, military commissioner of Wuping and administrator of Yongzhou, as the eldest of Xifan's brothers.

sentences.zh: 長直都指揮使劉彥瑫、天策府學士李弘皋、鄧懿文、小門使楊滌皆欲立希廣。

translations.literal: Chief director of the long guard Liu Yanchuang, Tiancefu academicians Li Honggao and Deng Yiwen, and junior gate commissioner Yang Di all wished to install Xi Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Chief director of the long guard Liu Yanchuang, Tiancefu academicians Li Honggao and Deng Yiwen, and junior gate commissioner Yang Di all favored enthroning Xiguang.

sentences.zh: 張少敵曰：「永州齒長而性剛，必不為都尉之下明矣。

translations.literal: Zhang Shaodi said, "Yongzhou is senior in age and stiff in temperament; clearly he will not serve under the commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shaodi said, "Yongzhou is older and headstrong—he will plainly not accept subordination to the commandant.

sentences.zh: 必立都尉，當思長策以制永州，使帖然不動則可。

translations.literal: If the commandant must be installed, you ought to devise a long-term plan to control Yongzhou and make him stay quiet—only then will it do.
translations.idiomatic: If you must enthrone the commandant, you need a long-term plan to keep Yongzhou in check and docile—only then will it work.

sentences.zh: 不然，社稷危矣。」

translations.literal: Otherwise the altars of state are in peril."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the realm itself is in danger."

sentences.zh: 彥瑫等不從。

translations.literal: Liu Yanchuang and the others did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanchuang and the others would not listen.

sentences.zh: 天策府學士拓跋恆曰：「三十五郎雖判軍府之政，然三十郎居長，請遣使以禮讓之。

translations.literal: Tiancefu academician Tuoba Heng said, "Although the thirty-fifth lord now administers the military government, the thirtieth lord is the elder—please send envoys to yield the position to him with proper ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Tiancefu academician Tuoba Heng said, "Though the thirty-fifth lord now runs the military government, the thirtieth lord is senior. Send envoys to yield the throne to him with proper ceremony.

sentences.zh: 不然，必起爭端。」

translations.literal: Otherwise strife is sure to arise."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise strife is certain to break out."

sentences.zh: 彥瑫等皆曰：「今日軍政在手，天與不取，使它人得之，異日吾輩安所自容乎！」

translations.literal: Liu Yanchuang and the others all said, "Today military and civil power are in our hands. Heaven gives and we do not take—if another obtains it, where shall we find room for ourselves another day!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanchuang and the rest said, "Military and civil power are in our hands today. Heaven offers and we refuse—if another takes the throne, where will we stand tomorrow!"

sentences.zh: 希廣懦弱，不能自決。

translations.literal: Xi Guang was weak and could not decide for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xiguang was timid and could not decide for himself.

sentences.zh: 乙未，彥瑫等稱希範遺命，共立之。

translations.literal: On yiwei Liu Yanchuang and the others, citing Xi Fan's testamentary command, jointly installed him.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei Liu Yanchuang and the others, citing Xifan's testamentary command, jointly enthroned him.

sentences.zh: 張少敵退而歎曰：「禍其始此乎！」

translations.literal: Zhang Shaodi withdrew and sighed, "Does calamity begin here?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shaodi withdrew and sighed, "Does disaster begin here?"

sentences.zh: 與拓跋恆皆稱疾不出。

translations.literal: He and Tuoba Heng both pleaded illness and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: He and Tuoba Heng both pleaded illness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 丙申，帝發太原，自陰地關出晉、絳。

translations.literal: On bingshen the emperor set out from Taiyuan and went out through Yindi Pass toward Jin and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen the emperor departed Taiyuan and marched out through Yindi Pass toward Jin and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，史弘肇奏克澤州。

translations.literal: On dingyou Shi Hongzhao reported the capture of Ze Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou Shi Hongzhao reported the capture of Ze Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 始，弘肇攻澤州，刺史翟令奇固守不下。

translations.literal: At the beginning Hongzhao attacked Ze Prefecture, but prefect Zhai Lingqi held firm and could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Hongzhao had attacked Ze Prefecture, but prefect Zhai Lingqi held firm and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 帝以弘肇兵少，欲召還。

translations.literal: The emperor thought Hongzhao's troops were few and wished to recall him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought Hongzhao's force was too small and wanted to recall him.

sentences.zh: 蘇逢吉、楊邠曰：「今陝、晉、河陽皆已向化，崔廷勳、耿崇美朝夕遁去；

translations.literal: Su Fengji and Yang Bin said, "Now Shaan, Jin, and Heyang have all submitted; Cui Tingxun and Geng Chongmei will flee before another day passes;
translations.idiomatic: Su Fengji and Yang Bin said, "Shaan, Jin, and Heyang have all submitted now. Cui Tingxun and Geng Chongmei will flee within days;

sentences.zh: 若召弘肇還，則河南人心動搖，虜勢復壯矣。」

translations.literal: if Hongzhao is recalled, the hearts of the people in Henan will waver and the barbarian power will grow strong again."
translations.idiomatic: if you recall Hongzhao, hearts in Henan will waver and Khitan strength will revive."

sentences.zh: 帝未決，使人諭指於弘肇。

translations.literal: The emperor had not decided and sent someone to convey his intent to Hongzhao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hesitated and sent a messenger to sound out Hongzhao.

sentences.zh: 弘肇曰：「兵已及此，勢如破竹，可進不可退。」

translations.literal: Hongzhao said, "The army has already reached this point; the momentum is like splitting bamboo—one can advance but not retreat."
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao said, "The army has come this far; momentum is like splitting bamboo—we can only advance, not retreat."

sentences.zh: 與逢吉等議合。

translations.literal: This accorded with Fengji's and the others' view.
translations.idiomatic: This matched Fengji's view and the rest.

sentences.zh: 帝乃從之。

translations.literal: The emperor then followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then agreed.

sentences.zh: 弘肇遣部將李萬超說令奇，令奇乃降。

translations.literal: Hongzhao sent his subordinate general Li Wanchao to persuade Lingqi, and Lingqi then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao sent his subordinate Li Wanchao to persuade Lingqi, and Lingqi surrendered.

sentences.zh: 弘肇以萬超權知澤州。

translations.literal: Hongzhao made Wanchao acting administrator of Ze Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao appointed Wanchao acting administrator of Ze Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 崔廷勳、耿崇美、奚王拽剌合兵逼河陽，張遇帥眾數千救之，戰於南阪，敗死。

translations.literal: Cui Tingxun, Geng Chongmei, and the Xi king Zhuaila united their armies to press Heyang. Zhang Yu led several thousand men to rescue it; they fought at South Slope, and Zhang was defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Tingxun, Geng Chongmei, and the Xi king Zhuaila combined forces to threaten Heyang. Zhang Yu led several thousand men to relieve the city; they fought at South Slope, and Zhang was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 武行德出戰，亦敗，閉城自守。

translations.literal: Wu Xingde went out to battle and was also defeated; he shut the city and held it himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xingde marched out to fight and was defeated as well; he shut the gates and held the city.

sentences.zh: 拽剌欲攻之，廷勳曰：「今北軍已去，得此何用！

translations.literal: Zhuaila wished to attack it. Tingxun said, "The northern army has already gone—what use is taking this!
translations.idiomatic: Zhuaila wanted to storm the city. Tingxun said, "The northern army has already withdrawn—what good is taking this place!

sentences.zh: 且殺一夫猶可惜，況一城乎！」

translations.literal: Moreover, to kill even one man is still a pity—how much more a whole city!"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, killing even one man is a pity—how much more an entire city!"

sentences.zh: 聞弘肇已得澤州，乃釋河陽，還保懷州。

translations.literal: Hearing that Hongzhao had already taken Ze Prefecture, they then released Heyang and withdrew to hold Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Hongzhao had taken Ze Prefecture, they abandoned Heyang and withdrew to defend Huai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 弘肇將至，廷勳等擁眾北遁，過衛州，大掠而去。

translations.literal: As Hongzhao was about to arrive, Tingxun and the others led their masses north in flight; passing through Wei Prefecture they plundered heavily and went on.
translations.idiomatic: As Hongzhao approached, Tingxun and the others fled north with their troops; passing through Wei Prefecture they looted heavily and continued on.

sentences.zh: 契丹在河南者相繼北去，弘肇引兵與武行德合。

translations.literal: The Khitan in Henan withdrew north one after another, and Hongzhao led his troops to join Wu Xingde.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan in Henan withdrew north in succession, and Hongzhao joined forces with Wu Xingde.

sentences.zh: 弘肇為人，沉毅寡言，御眾嚴整，將校小不從命，立撾殺之。

translations.literal: Hongzhao as a man was deep, resolute, and sparing of words; in commanding troops he was strict and orderly, and if officers great or small did not obey orders he had them beaten to death on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao was deep, resolute, and sparing of speech. He commanded with iron discipline: any officer who disobeyed, however minor the offense, was beaten to death on the spot.

sentences.zh: 士卒所過，犯民田及繫馬於樹者，皆斬之。

translations.literal: Wherever the soldiers passed, those who trespassed on the people's fields or tied their horses to trees were all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever his soldiers marched, anyone who trampled farmland or tied a horse to a tree was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 軍中惕息，莫敢犯令，故所向必克。

translations.literal: Within the army there was fearful silence; none dared violate the orders, and therefore wherever they went they were sure to prevail.
translations.idiomatic: The army trembled before him; none dared break discipline, and so they prevailed wherever they marched.

sentences.zh: 帝自晉陽安行入洛及汴，兵不血刃，皆弘肇之力也。

translations.literal: The emperor from Jinyang entered Luoyang and Bian in safety without the army staining a blade—all this was Hongzhao's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marched safely from Jinyang into Luoyang and Bian without shedding blood—all owing to Hongzhao.

sentences.zh: 帝由是倚愛之。

translations.literal: The emperor for this reason relied on and favored him.
translations.idiomatic: From this the emperor came to rely on and favor him.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，帝至霍邑，遣使諭河中節度使趙匡贊，仍以契丹囚其父延壽告之。

translations.literal: On xinchou the emperor reached Huoyi and sent envoys to instruct Hedong Military Commissioner Zhao Kuangzan, also informing him that the Khitan held his father Yanshou prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou the emperor reached Huoyi and sent envoys to Hedong military commissioner Zhao Kuangzan, informing him as well that the Khitan held his father Yanshou prisoner.

sentences.zh: 滋德宮有宮人五十餘人，蕭翰欲取之，宦者張環不與。

translations.literal: At Zide Palace there were more than fifty palace women. Xiao Han wished to take them, but eunuch Zhang Huan would not give them up.
translations.idiomatic: Zide Palace held more than fifty palace women. Xiao Han wanted to seize them, but eunuch Zhang Huan refused.

sentences.zh: 翰破鎖奪宮人，執環，燒鐵灼之，腹爛而死。

translations.literal: Han broke the lock and seized the palace women, seized Huan, burned iron to scald him, and his belly rotted until he died.
translations.idiomatic: Han broke the locks, seized the women, seized Huan, and burned him with red-hot iron until his belly rotted and he died.

sentences.zh: 初，翰聞帝擁兵而南，欲北歸。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Han heard that the emperor was leading troops south, he wished to return north.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Han heard that the emperor was marching south with an army, he wished to return north.

sentences.zh: 恐中國無主，必大亂，己不得從容而去。

translations.literal: He feared that if China had no ruler there would surely be great disorder and he would not be able to depart at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: He feared that without a ruler in China there would be chaos and he could not withdraw at leisure.

sentences.zh: 時唐明宗子許王從益與王淑妃在洛陽，翰遣高謨翰迎之，矯稱契丹主命，又以從益知南朝軍國事，召己赴恆州。

translations.literal: At that time Tang Emperor Mingzong's son Prince Xu Li Congyi and Consort Wang were in Luoyang. Han sent Gao Mohan to welcome them, falsely claiming it was the Khitan ruler's command, and also had Congyi oversee the military and civil affairs of the Southern Court and summoned himself to Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Emperor Mingzong's son Prince Xu Li Congyi and Consort Wang were then in Luoyang. Han sent Gao Mohan to fetch them, falsely claiming Khitan orders, installed Congyi to oversee the Southern Court's military and civil affairs, and summoned himself to Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 淑妃、從益匿於徽陵下宮，不得已而出。

translations.literal: Consort Wang and Congyi hid in the lower palace at Huiling but, having no alternative, came out.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wang and Congyi hid in the lower palace at Huiling but had no choice but to emerge.

sentences.zh: 至大梁，翰立以為帝，帥諸酋長拜之，以禮部尚書王松、御史中丞趙遠為宰相，前宣徽使甄城翟光鄴為樞密使，左金吾大將軍王景崇為宣徽使，以北來指揮使劉祚權侍衛親軍都指揮使，充在京巡檢。

translations.literal: When they reached Daliang, Han installed Congyi as emperor, led the various chieftains to bow to him, made Minister of Rites Wang Song and Censor-in-Chief Zhao Yuan chancellors, former commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service Zhai Guangye of Zhencheng as commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Left Golden Crow General Wang Jingchong as commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service, and northern-come commander Liu Zuo as acting commander of the Palace Attendant Army and inspector in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At Daliang Han enthroned Congyi, led the chieftains to bow to him, appointed Minister of Rites Wang Song and censor-in-chief Zhao Yuan as chancellors, former palace domestic service commissioner Zhai Guangye of Zhencheng as bureau of military affairs commissioner, Left Golden Crow general Wang Jingchong as palace domestic service commissioner, and northern commander Liu Zuo as acting commander of the palace attendant army and capital inspector.

sentences.zh: 松，徽之子也。

translations.literal: Song was the son of Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Song was the son of Hui.

sentences.zh: 百官謁見淑妃，淑妃泣曰：「吾母子單弱如此，而為諸公所推，是禍吾家也！」

translations.literal: The hundred officials paid homage to Consort Wang. She wept and said, "My son and I are so weak and alone, yet you gentlemen have pushed us forward—this is bringing calamity on our house!"
translations.idiomatic: The officials paid homage to Consort Wang. She wept and said, "My son and I are so helpless, yet you gentlemen have pushed us forward—this will bring ruin on our house!"

sentences.zh: 翰留燕兵千人守諸門，為從益宿衛。

translations.literal: Han left a thousand Yan troops to guard the various gates as Congyi's night guard.
translations.idiomatic: Han left a thousand Yan troops to guard the gates as Congyi's night guard.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，翰及劉晞辭行，從益餞於北郊。

translations.literal: On renyin Han and Liu Xi took leave to depart; Congyi entertained them at the northern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Han and Liu Xi took their leave to depart; Congyi entertained them at the northern suburb.

sentences.zh: 遣使召高行周於宋州，武行德於河陽，皆不至。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to summon Gao Xingzhou at Song Prefecture and Wu Xingde at Heyang; neither came.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to summon Gao Xingzhou at Song Prefecture and Wu Xingde at Heyang; neither came.

sentences.zh: 淑妃懼，召大臣謀之曰：「吾母子為蕭翰所逼，分當滅亡。

translations.literal: Consort Wang was afraid and summoned the great ministers to deliberate, saying, "My son and I were forced by Xiao Han; by rights we ought to perish.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wang grew afraid and summoned the ministers, saying, "My son and I were forced by Xiao Han—we deserve to perish.

sentences.zh: 諸公無罪，宜早迎新主，自求多福，勿以吾母子為意！」

translations.literal: You gentlemen are without guilt; you ought early to welcome the new ruler and seek your own greater fortune—do not consider my son and me!"
translations.idiomatic: You are innocent. Welcome the new ruler early and secure your own fortunes—do not spare a thought for us!"

sentences.zh: 眾感其言，皆未忍叛去。

translations.literal: The crowd was moved by her words and none could bear to rebel and leave.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly was moved by her words and none could bring himself to defect.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「今集諸營，不減五千，與燕兵並力堅守一月，北救必至。」

translations.literal: Someone said, "If we now gather the various camps, there are no fewer than five thousand; together with the Yan troops we can hold firm for a month, and northern rescue is sure to arrive."
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "If we gather the camps now we have at least five thousand men. Together with the Yan troops we can hold for a month—northern relief will surely come."

sentences.zh: 淑妃曰：「吾母子亡國之餘，安敢與人爭天下！

translations.literal: Consort Wang said, "My son and I are the remnant of a perished state—how dare we contend with others for the realm!
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wang said, "My son and I are the wreckage of a fallen house—how dare we contend for the realm!

sentences.zh: 不幸至此，死生惟人所裁。

translations.literal: Having come unhappily to this, life and death are for others to decide.
translations.idiomatic: Having come to this pass, our lives are for others to dispose of.

sentences.zh: 若新主見察，當知我無所負。

translations.literal: If the new ruler sees clearly, he will know that we have done nothing to betray him.
translations.idiomatic: If the new ruler understands, he will know we have done nothing wrong.

sentences.zh: 今更為計畫，則禍及他人，闔城塗炭，終何益乎！」

translations.literal: If we now make further plans, calamity will reach others and the whole city will be scorched—what good would it do in the end!"
translations.idiomatic: If we plot further, others will suffer and the whole city will burn—what good would that do!"

sentences.zh: 眾猶欲拒守，三司使文安劉審交曰：「余燕人，豈不為燕兵計！

translations.literal: The crowd still wished to resist and hold. Commissioner of the Three Departments Liu Shenjiao of Wen'an said, "I am a Yan man myself—would I not plan for the Yan troops!
translations.idiomatic: The assembly still wanted to resist. Commissioner of the Three Departments Liu Shenjiao of Wen'an said, "I am a Yan man myself—would I not plan for the Yan troops!

sentences.zh: 顧事有不可如何者。

translations.literal: But when affairs cannot be otherwise, what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: But when affairs cannot be helped, what can one do?

sentences.zh: 今城中大亂之餘，公私窮竭，遺民無幾，若復受圍一月，無□類矣。

translations.literal: Now after the great disorder in the city, public and private resources are exhausted and the surviving people are few; if we are besieged again for a month, there will be no [survivors] left.
translations.idiomatic: After the chaos in the city, public and private stores are exhausted and few people remain. If we are besieged another month, no one will be left alive.

sentences.zh: 願諸公勿復言，一從太妃處分。」

translations.literal: I wish you gentlemen would speak no more and all follow the senior consort's disposition."
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to say no more and follow the senior consort's decision."

sentences.zh: 乃用趙遠、翟光鄴策，稱梁王，知軍國事。

translations.literal: Thereupon they adopted Zhao Yuan's and Zhai Guangye's plan, styled him Prince of Liang, and had him oversee military and civil affairs.
translations.idiomatic: They then adopted Zhao Yuan's and Zhai Guangye's plan, styled Congyi Prince of Liang, and put him in charge of military and civil affairs.

sentences.zh: 遣使奉表稱臣迎帝，請早赴京師，仍出居私第。

translations.literal: They sent envoys with a memorial declaring themselves subjects to welcome the emperor, asking that he come early to the capital, while they themselves moved out to a private residence.
translations.idiomatic: They sent envoys with a memorial of submission to welcome the emperor, urging him to come quickly to the capital, while they themselves withdrew to a private residence.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，帝至晉州。

translations.literal: On jiachen the emperor reached Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen the emperor reached Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 契丹主兀欲以契丹主德光有子在國，己以兄子襲位，又無述律太后之命，擅自立，內不自安。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler Wuyu, because the Khitan ruler Deguang had a son in the state and he himself had succeeded to the throne as a nephew's son, and moreover without the command of Empress Dowager Shulü had established himself on his own authority, was inwardly ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor Yelü Ruan felt insecure on the throne: Deguang still had a son in the realm, Ruan himself had seized succession as a nephew rather than a son, and he had taken the throne without authorization from Empress Dowager Shulü.

sentences.zh: 初，契丹主阿保機卒於勃海，述律太后殺酋長及諸將凡數百人。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Khitan ruler Abaoji died in Bohai, Empress Dowager Shulü killed chieftains and generals, several hundred in all.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Abaoji of Khitan died in Bohai, Empress Dowager Shulü had put to death several hundred chieftains and generals.

sentences.zh: 契丹主德光復卒於境外，酋長諸將懼死，乃謀奉契丹主兀欲勒兵北歸。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler Deguang again died beyond the borders; the chieftains and generals, fearing death, thereupon plotted to support the Khitan ruler Wuyu in leading the army north in return.
translations.idiomatic: When Deguang in turn died abroad, the chieftains and generals, fearing for their lives, plotted to install Yelü Ruan and march the army back north.

sentences.zh: 契丹主以安國節度使麻荅為中京留守，以前武州刺史高奉明為安國節度使。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler appointed Anguo military commissioner Mada as defender of the Central Capital and the former Wuzhou prefect Gao Fengming as Anguo military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan left Mada, military commissioner of Anguo, as defender of the Central Capital and appointed the former prefect of Wuzhou, Gao Fengming, military commissioner of Anguo.

sentences.zh: 晉文武官及士窣窸留於恆州，獨以翰林學士徐台符、李澣及後宮、宦者、教坊人自隨。

translations.literal: The Jin civil and military officials and the gentry and commoners were left at Hengzhou; he took with him only the Hanlin academicians Xu Taifu and Li Huan, together with the inner palace, eunuchs, and entertainers of the music office.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Jin civil and military officials and the gentry and common folk at Hengzhou, taking with him only the Hanlin academicians Xu Taifu and Li Huan, the inner palace, eunuchs, and musicians of the entertainment bureau.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，發真定。

translations.literal: On yisi he set out from Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi he departed Zhending.

sentences.zh: 帝之即位也，絳州刺史李從朗與契丹將成霸卿等拒命，帝遣西南面招討使、護國節度使白文珂攻之，未下。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, Jiang Prefecture prefect Li Conglang together with the Khitan general Cheng Baqing and others defied orders; the emperor sent the southwestern campaign commissioner and Huguo military commissioner Bai Wenke to attack them, but the city was not taken.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first took the throne, Jiang Prefecture prefect Li Conglang and the Khitan general Cheng Baqing and others refused to submit. The emperor sent southwestern campaign commissioner and Huguo military commissioner Bai Wenke against them, but the city did not fall.

sentences.zh: 帝至城下，命諸軍四布而勿攻，以利害諭之。

translations.literal: The emperor reached the foot of the city, ordered the armies to deploy on four sides without attacking, and instructed them on advantage and harm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came to the city, arrayed his forces on all four sides without assaulting, and explained to the defenders what they stood to gain or lose.

sentences.zh: 戊申，從朗舉城降。

translations.literal: On wushen Conglang surrendered the whole city.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Conglang surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 帝命親將分護諸門，士卒一人毋得入。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered his personal generals to guard the gates separately; not a single soldier was permitted to enter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had his own generals guard each gate in turn and forbade any soldier from entering.

sentences.zh: 以偏將薛瓊為防禦使。

translations.literal: He appointed the subordinate general Xue Qiong defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed subordinate general Xue Qiong defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，帝至陝州，趙暉自御帝馬而入。

translations.literal: On xinhai the emperor reached Shan Prefecture; Zhao Hui himself drove the emperor's horse as they entered.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai the emperor reached Shan Prefecture. Zhao Hui took the reins of the emperor's horse and led him in.

sentences.zh: 壬子，至石壕，汴人有來迎者。

translations.literal: On renzi he reached Shihao; people of Bian came out to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi he reached Shihao, where people from Bian came out to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 六月，甲寅朔，蕭翰至恆州，與麻荅以鐵騎圍張礪之第。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on jiayin the first day of the month, Xiao Han reached Hengzhou and, with Mada, surrounded Zhang Li's residence with iron cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the first day (jiayin), Xiao Han reached Hengzhou and, with Mada, surrounded Zhang Li's residence with armored cavalry.

sentences.zh: 礪方臥病，出見之，翰數之曰：「汝何故言於先帝，雲胡人不可以為節度使？

translations.literal: Li was then lying ill; he came out to see them. Han reproached him, saying, "Why did you tell the late emperor that barbarians cannot serve as military commissioners?
translations.idiomatic: Li was ill in bed but came out to see them. Han berated him: "Why did you tell the late emperor that Khitan men must not be made military commissioners?

sentences.zh: 又，吾為宣武節度使，且國舅也，汝在中書乃帖我！

translations.literal: Moreover, I am Xuanwu military commissioner and also the emperor's uncle by marriage—yet you in the Secretariat posted notices against me!
translations.idiomatic: And I am military commissioner of Xuanwu and the emperor's uncle by marriage—yet you in the Secretariat posted orders against me!

sentences.zh: 又，先帝留我守汴州，令我處宮中，汝以為不可。

translations.literal: Again, the late emperor left me to guard Bianzhou and allowed me to dwell in the palace—you said that was not permissible.
translations.idiomatic: Again, the late emperor left me to guard Bian and let me live in the palace—you said that was wrong.

sentences.zh: 又，譖我及解裡於先帝，雲解裡好掠人財，我好掠人子女。

translations.literal: Again, you slandered me and Jieli to the late emperor, saying Jieli loved to plunder people's wealth and I loved to plunder people's sons and daughters.
translations.idiomatic: And you slandered me and Jieli to the late emperor, saying Jieli loved to seize people's property and I loved to seize their sons and daughters.

sentences.zh: 今我必殺汝！」

translations.literal: Now I will certainly kill you!"
translations.idiomatic: Now I will kill you!"

sentences.zh: 命鎖之。

translations.literal: He ordered him shackled.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Li shackled.

sentences.zh: 礪抗聲曰：「此皆國家大體，吾實言之。

translations.literal: Li answered in a defiant voice, "These were all matters of great state principle; I spoke the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Li answered boldly, "These were all matters of fundamental state policy—I spoke the truth.

sentences.zh: 欲殺即殺，奚以鎖為！」

translations.literal: If you wish to kill, then kill—why bother with shackles!"
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to kill me, kill me—why put me in chains!"

sentences.zh: 麻荅以大臣不可專殺，力救止之，翰乃釋之。

translations.literal: Mada, on the grounds that a great minister could not be killed on one's own authority, strove to save and stop it; Han thereupon released him.
translations.idiomatic: Mada argued that a senior minister could not be executed without authority and pressed hard to stop it; Han then released him.

sentences.zh: 是夕，礪憤恚而卒。

translations.literal: That evening Li died of indignation and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: That night Li died of rage and grief.

sentences.zh: 崔廷勳見麻荅，趨走拜，起，跪而獻酒，麻荅踞而受之。

translations.literal: Cui Tingxun, on seeing Mada, ran forward and bowed; rising, he knelt and presented wine; Mada sat with legs spread and received it.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Tingxun saw Mada, he ran forward and bowed, then knelt and offered wine. Mada sat with legs sprawled and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，帝至新安，西京留司官悉來迎。

translations.literal: On yimao the emperor reached Xin'an; all the Western Capital officials left on duty came to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao the emperor reached Xin'an, where every Western Capital official on duty came out to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 吳越忠獻王弘佐卒。

translations.literal: Hong Zuo, King Zhongxian of Wuyue, died.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zuo, King Zhongxian of Wuyue, died.

sentences.zh: 遺令以丞相弘倧為鎮海、鎮東節度使兼侍中。

translations.literal: His testamentary order made the chief minister Hong Zong military commissioner of Zhenhai and Zhendong and concurrently palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In his final instructions he named chief minister Hong Zong military commissioner of Zhenhai and Zhendong and concurrent palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，帝至洛陽，入居宮中，汴州百官奉表來迎。

translations.literal: On bingchen the emperor reached Luoyang, entered and dwelt in the palace, and the officials of Bianzhou presented memorials coming to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen the emperor reached Luoyang and took up residence in the palace. Officials from Bian presented memorials welcoming him.

sentences.zh: 詔諭以受契丹補署者皆勿自疑，聚其告牒而焚之。

translations.literal: An edict instructed that all who had received Khitan supplementary appointments should not doubt themselves; their commission documents were gathered and burned.
translations.idiomatic: An edict assured everyone who had accepted appointments from the Khitan that they need not fear; their commission documents were collected and burned.

sentences.zh: 趙遠更名上交。

translations.literal: Zhao Yuan changed his name to Shangjiao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yuan changed his name to Shangjiao.

sentences.zh: 命鄭州防禦使郭從義先入大梁清宮，密令殺李從益及王淑妃。

translations.literal: He ordered Zhengzhou defense commissioner Guo Congyi to enter Daliang first and clear the palace, and secretly commanded the killing of Li Congyi and Consort Wang.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Zhengzhou defense commissioner Guo Congyi to enter Daliang ahead of him and clear the palace, secretly instructing him to kill Li Congyi and Consort Wang.

sentences.zh: 淑妃且死，曰：「吾兒為契丹所立，何罪而死！

translations.literal: As Consort Wang was about to die, she said, "My son was established by the Khitan—what crime is there in dying!
translations.idiomatic: As Consort Wang faced death, she said, "My son was set on the throne by the Khitan—what crime warrants death!

sentences.zh: 何不留之，使每歲寒食，以一盂麥飯灑明宗陵乎！」

translations.literal: Why not spare him, so that every year at Cold Food Festival a bowl of wheat meal might be sprinkled on Emperor Mingzong's tomb!"
translations.idiomatic: Why not spare him, so that each Cold Food Festival he might offer a bowl of wheat meal at Emperor Mingzong's tomb!"

sentences.zh: 聞者泣下。

translations.literal: Those who heard wept.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard her wept.

sentences.zh: 戊午，帝發洛陽。

translations.literal: On wuwu the emperor set out from Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu the emperor departed Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 樞密院吏魏仁浦自契丹逃歸，見於鞏。

translations.literal: Wei Renpu, a clerk of the Bureau of Military Affairs, fled back from the Khitan and was received at Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Renpu, a clerk of the Bureau of Military Affairs, escaped from Khitan territory and was received at Gong.

sentences.zh: 郭威問以兵數及故事，仁浦強記精敏，威由是親任之。

translations.literal: Guo Wei questioned him on troop numbers and precedents; Renpu had a powerful memory and was keenly sharp, and Wei thereupon entrusted him closely.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei questioned him about troop strengths and precedent. Renpu's memory was exceptional and his mind acute, and from that time Wei relied on him closely.

sentences.zh: 仁浦，衛州人也。

translations.literal: Renpu was a man of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Renpu was a native of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，汴州百官竇貞固等迎於滎陽。

translations.literal: On xinyou the officials of Bianzhou, Dou Zhengu and others, welcomed him at Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou Dou Zhengu and the other officials of Bian welcomed the emperor at Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 甲子，帝至大梁，晉之籓鎮相繼來降。

translations.literal: On jiazi the emperor reached Daliang; the Jin frontier commands came to surrender one after another.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the emperor reached Daliang, and the former Jin military districts submitted in succession.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，吳越王弘倧襲位。

translations.literal: On bingyin King Hong Zong of Wuyue succeeded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Hong Zong succeeded as king of Wuyue.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，帝下詔大赦。

translations.literal: On wuchen the emperor issued an edict of general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen the emperor proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 凡契丹所除節度使，下至將吏，各安職任，不復變更。

translations.literal: All military commissioners appointed by the Khitan, down to generals and clerks, were each to keep their posts without further change.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone the Khitan had appointed—from military commissioners down to officers and clerks—was to keep his post without change.

sentences.zh: 復以汴州為東京，改國號曰漢，仍稱天福年，曰：「余未忍忘晉也。」

translations.literal: Bianzhou was again made the Eastern Capital; the state designation was changed to Han, yet the reign title Tianfu was still used. He said, "I cannot yet bear to forget Jin."
translations.idiomatic: He restored Bian as the Eastern Capital, changed the dynastic name to Han, and kept the Tianfu reign era, saying, "I cannot yet bring myself to forget Jin."

sentences.zh: 復青、襄、汝三節度。

translations.literal: The three commands of Qing, Xiang, and Ru were restored.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the three military districts of Qing, Xiang, and Ru.

sentences.zh: 壬申，以北京留守崇為河東節度使，同平章事。

translations.literal: On renshen Beijing defender Chong was made Hedong military commissioner and concurrent co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen Liu Chong, defender of Beijing, was appointed Hedong military commissioner and concurrent co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 契丹述律太后聞契丹主自立，大怒，發兵拒之。

translations.literal: Khitan Empress Dowager Shulü, hearing that the Khitan ruler had established himself on his own, was greatly angered and sent troops to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Shulü learned that Yelü Ruan had seized the throne on his own, she was furious and sent troops against him.

sentences.zh: 契丹主以偉王為前鋒，相遇於石橋。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler took Prince Wei as vanguard; they met at Shiqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan advanced with Prince Wei as vanguard and met her forces at Shiqiao.

sentences.zh: 初，晉侍衛馬軍都指揮使李彥韜從晉主北遷，隸述律太后麾下，太后以為排陳使。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jin Palace Guard cavalry commander Li Yantao had followed the Jin ruler north in relocation and served under Empress Dowager Shulü; the empress dowager made him battle-array commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Jin Palace Guard cavalry commander Li Yantao had followed the Jin court north and served under Empress Dowager Shulü, who appointed him battle-array commissioner.

sentences.zh: 彥韜迎降於偉王，太后兵由是大敗。

translations.literal: Yantao came forward and surrendered to Prince Wei; the empress dowager's army was thereby greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Yantao went over to Prince Wei, and the empress dowager's army was routed.

sentences.zh: 契丹主幽太后於阿保機墓。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler confined the empress dowager at Abaoji's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan confined the empress dowager at Abaoji's tomb.

sentences.zh: 改元天祿，自稱天授皇帝，以高勳為樞密使。

translations.literal: He changed the era name to Tianlu, styled himself Emperor Tian Shou, and appointed Gao Xun bureau commissioner of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He changed the era name to Tianlu, styled himself Emperor Tian Shou, and appointed Gao Xun bureau commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 契丹主慕中華風俗，多用晉臣，而荒於酒色，輕慢諸酋長，由是國人不附，諸部數叛，興兵誅討，故數年之間，不暇南寇。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler admired Chinese customs and employed many Jin ministers, yet he was dissolute in wine and women and treated the chieftains lightly; thereby the people of the state did not attach themselves to him, the various tribes rebelled repeatedly, and he raised troops to punish and suppress them—so that for several years he had no leisure to raid south.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan admired Chinese ways and employed many former Jin ministers, but he indulged in wine and women and slighted the chieftains. The Khitan people lost heart, tribes rebelled again and again, and he spent years campaigning against them—so for several years he had no leisure to raid the south.

sentences.zh: 初，契丹主德光命奉國都指揮使南宮王繼弘、都虞候樊暉以所部兵戍相州，彰德節度使高唐英善待之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Khitan ruler Deguang had ordered Fengguo army commander Wang Jihong of Nangong and chief adjutant Fan Hui to garrison Xiang Prefecture with their troops; Zhangde military commissioner Gao Tangying treated them well.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Deguang had ordered Fengguo army commander Wang Jihong of Nangong and chief adjutant Fan Hui to garrison Xiang Prefecture with their troops. Zhangde military commissioner Gao Tangying treated them generously.

sentences.zh: 戍兵無鎧仗，唐英以鎧仗給之，倚信如親戚。

translations.literal: The garrison troops had no armor and weapons; Tangying supplied them with armor and weapons and relied on them as on kin.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison lacked armor and arms; Tangying supplied them and trusted them as kin.

sentences.zh: 唐英聞帝南下，舉鎮請降。

translations.literal: Tangying, hearing that the emperor was marching south, offered the whole command in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Tangying heard that the emperor was marching south, he offered his whole command in submission.

sentences.zh: 使者未返，繼弘、暉殺唐英。

translations.literal: Before the envoy had returned, Jihong and Hui killed Tangying.
translations.idiomatic: Before the envoy returned, Jihong and Hui killed Tangying.

sentences.zh: 繼弘自稱留後，遣使告雲唐英反覆，詔以繼弘為彰德留後。

translations.literal: Jihong styled himself acting commissioner and sent an envoy reporting that Tangying had been treacherous; an edict appointed Jihong acting Zhangde commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Jihong declared himself acting commissioner and sent word that Tangying had been treacherous. An edict made Jihong acting commissioner of Zhangde.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以暉為磁州刺史。

translations.literal: On gengchen Hui was made prefect of Ci Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen Hui was appointed prefect of Ci.

sentences.zh: 安國節度使高奉明聞唐英死，心不自安，請於麻荅，署馬步都指揮使劉鐸為節度副使，知軍府事，身歸恆州。

translations.literal: Anguo military commissioner Gao Fengming, hearing of Tangying's death, was inwardly ill at ease; he requested of Mada that horse-and-foot commander Liu Duo be appointed deputy military commissioner to oversee military administration, and he himself returned to Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Fengming, military commissioner of Anguo, heard of Tangying's death, he grew uneasy. He asked Mada to appoint horse-and-foot commander Liu Duo deputy military commissioner to run the headquarters and returned to Hengzhou himself.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使告諭荊南。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to announce and instruct Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to announce his accession to Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 高從誨上表賀，且求郢州，帝不許。

translations.literal: Gao Conghui presented a memorial of congratulation and also requested Ying Prefecture; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Conghui sent a congratulatory memorial and asked for Ying Prefecture; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 及加恩使至，拒而不受。

translations.literal: When the envoy bearing additional favor arrived, he refused and would not receive him.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy bearing additional honors arrived, he refused to receive him.

sentences.zh: 唐主聞契丹主德光卒，蕭翰棄大梁去，下詔曰：「乃眷中原，本朝故地。」

translations.literal: The Tang ruler, hearing that the Khitan ruler Deguang had died and Xiao Han had abandoned Daliang and left, issued an edict saying, "We look back fondly on the Central Plains—the former territory of our court."
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang ruler learned that Deguang was dead and Xiao Han had abandoned Daliang, he issued an edict: "We look back fondly on the Central Plains—the former territory of our court."

sentences.zh: 以左右衛聖統軍、忠武節度使、同平章事李金全為北面行營招討使，議經略北方。

translations.literal: He appointed Left and Right Weisheng army commander-in-chief, Zhongwu military commissioner, and concurrent co-director Li Jinquan northern campaign commissioner to discuss strategy for the north.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Li Jinquan—commander-in-chief of the Left and Right Weisheng armies, Zhongwu military commissioner, and concurrent co-director—northern campaign commissioner to plan operations in the north.

sentences.zh: 聞帝已入大梁，遂不敢出兵。

translations.literal: Hearing that the emperor had already entered Daliang, he thereupon did not dare to send out troops.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that the emperor had already entered Daliang, he did not dare march.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，甲午，以馬希廣為天策上將軍、武安節度使、江南諸道都統，兼中書令，封楚王。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on jiawu Ma Xiguang was made celestial strategy general-in-chief, Wu'an military commissioner, overall commander of the Jiangnan circuits, concurrently chief minister of the Secretariat, and enfeoffed as Prince of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on jiawu Ma Xiguang was appointed celestial strategy general-in-chief, Wu'an military commissioner, overall commander of the Jiangnan circuits, concurrent chief minister of the Secretariat, and enfeoffed as Prince of Chu.

sentences.zh: 或傳趙延壽已死。

translations.literal: Some reported that Zhao Yanshou was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor had it that Zhao Yanshou was dead.

sentences.zh: 郭威言於帝曰：「趙匡贊，契丹所署，今猶在河中，宜遣使弔祭，因起復移鎮。

translations.literal: Guo Wei said to the emperor, "Zhao Kuangzan, appointed by the Khitan, is still at Hezhong; it would be fitting to send envoys to mourn and sacrifice, and thereby recall him to office and transfer his command.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei said to the emperor, "Zhao Kuangzan, whom the Khitan appointed, is still at Hezhong. We should send envoys to offer condolences and, in the course of recalling him to office, transfer his command.

sentences.zh: 彼既家國無歸，必感恩承命。」

translations.literal: Since he has no home or state to return to, he will surely be grateful and accept the command."
translations.idiomatic: With no homeland to return to, he will surely accept out of gratitude."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 會鄴都留守、天雄節度使兼中書令杜重威、天平節度使兼侍中李守貞皆奉表歸命。

translations.literal: It happened that Yedu defender, Tianxiong military commissioner, and concurrent chief minister Du Chongwei, and Tianping military commissioner and concurrent palace attendant Li Shouzhen, both presented memorials submitting to orders.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Du Chongwei—Yedu defender, Tianxiong military commissioner, and concurrent chief minister—and Li Shouzhen—Tianping military commissioner and concurrent palace attendant—both submitted memorials of allegiance.

sentences.zh: 重威仍請移它鎮。

translations.literal: Chongwei further requested transfer to another command.
translations.idiomatic: Chongwei also asked to be transferred to another post.

sentences.zh: 歸德節度使兼中書令高行周入朝，丙申，徙重威為歸德節度使，以行周代之；

translations.literal: Guide military commissioner and concurrent chief minister Gao Xingzhou entered court; on bingchen Chongwei was transferred to be Guide military commissioner and Xingzhou replaced him;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xingzhou, Guide military commissioner and concurrent chief minister, came to court. On bingchen Chongwei was transferred to Guide military commissioner and Xingzhou took his place;

sentences.zh: 守貞為護國節度使，加兼中書令；

translations.literal: Shouzhen was made Huguo military commissioner and additionally given concurrent chief ministership;
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen was made Huguo military commissioner and given concurrent chief ministership;

sentences.zh: 徙護國節度使趙匡贊為晉昌節度使。

translations.literal: Huguo military commissioner Zhao Kuangzan was transferred to be Jinchang military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: and Huguo military commissioner Zhao Kuangzan was transferred to Jinchang military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 後二年，延壽始卒於契丹。

translations.literal: Two years later Yanshou finally died among the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Yanshou did in fact die in Khitan territory.

sentences.zh: 吳越王弘倧以其弟台州刺史弘俶同參相府事。

translations.literal: King Hong Zong of Wuyue had his younger brother Hong Chu, Taizhou prefect, participate together in the affairs of the chief minister's office.
translations.idiomatic: King Hong Zong of Wuyue had his younger brother Hong Chu, prefect of Taizhou, join him in managing the chief minister's office.

sentences.zh: 李達以其弟通知福州留後，自詣錢唐見吳越王弘倧，弘倧承製加達兼侍中，更其名曰孺贇。

translations.literal: Li Da had his younger brother inform the acting commissioner of Fuzhou; he himself went to Qiantang to see King Hong Zong of Wuyue. Hong Zong, by imperial rescript, additionally made Da concurrent palace attendant and changed his name to Ruyun.
translations.idiomatic: Li Da left his younger brother to notify the acting commissioner of Fuzhou and went himself to Qiantang to see King Hong Zong. Hong Zong, by imperial rescript, made Da concurrent palace attendant and changed his name to Ruyun.

sentences.zh: 既而孺贇悔懼，以金筍二十株及雜寶賂內牙統軍使胡進思，求歸福州。

translations.literal: Before long Ruyun felt regret and fear; with twenty golden bamboo shoots and miscellaneous treasures he bribed inner-gate army commander Hu Jinsi, seeking to return to Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Ruyun grew fearful and regretful. He bribed inner-gate army commander Hu Jinsi with twenty golden bamboo shoots and other treasures, asking to return to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 進思為之請，弘倧從之。

translations.literal: Jinsi pleaded on his behalf, and Hong Zong consented.
translations.idiomatic: Jinsi interceded for him, and Hong Zong agreed.

sentences.zh: 杜重威自以附契丹，負中國，內常疑懼。

translations.literal: Du Chongwei, considering that he had attached himself to the Khitan and betrayed China, was inwardly often fearful and apprehensive.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chongwei knew he had sided with the Khitan and betrayed China, and he lived in constant fear.

sentences.zh: 及移鎮制下，復拒而不受，遣其子弘璲質於麻荅以求援。

translations.literal: When the order transferring his command was issued, he again refused and would not accept it, sending his son Hongji as hostage to Mada to seek aid.
translations.idiomatic: When the transfer order arrived, he refused it again and sent his son Hongji to Mada as a hostage to seek Khitan aid.

sentences.zh: 趙延壽有幽州親兵二千在恆州，指揮使張璉將之，重威請以守魏。

translations.literal: Zhao Yanshou had two thousand personal troops from Youzhou at Hengzhou, commanded by Zhang Lian; Chongwei requested that they be used to hold Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshou had two thousand personal troops from Youzhou at Hengzhou under commander Zhang Lian; Chongwei asked that they be sent to hold Wei.

sentences.zh: 麻荅遣其將楊袞將契丹千五百人及幽州兵赴之。

translations.literal: Mada sent his general Yang Gun to lead fifteen hundred Khitan and the Youzhou troops to go to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: Mada sent his general Yang Gun with fifteen hundred Khitan and the Youzhou troops to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 閏月，庚午，詔削奪重威官爵，以高行周為招討使，鎮寧節度使慕容彥超副之，以討重威。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on gengwu an edict stripped Chongwei of office and rank; Gao Xingzhou was made campaign commissioner and Zhenning military commissioner Murong Yanchao his deputy, to campaign against Chongwei.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on gengwu an edict stripped Chongwei of rank and office. Gao Xingzhou was made campaign commissioner with Zhenning military commissioner Murong Yanchao as deputy to attack him.

sentences.zh: 辛未，楊邠、郭威、王章皆為正使。

translations.literal: On xinwei Yang Bin, Guo Wei, and Wang Zhang were all made chief commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Yang Bin, Guo Wei, and Wang Zhang were all appointed chief commissioners.

sentences.zh: 時兵荒之餘，公私匱竭，北來兵與朝廷兵合，頓增數倍。

translations.literal: At that time, in the aftermath of military devastation, public and private stores were exhausted; the northern troops combined with the court armies instantly increased several fold.
translations.idiomatic: After the devastation of war, public and private stores were empty. When the northern armies joined the court forces, the burden instantly multiplied several times over.

sentences.zh: 章白帝罷不急之務，省無益之費以奉軍，用度克贍。

translations.literal: Zhang informed the emperor to stop non-urgent affairs and reduce unprofitable expenditures to supply the army; expenses were thereby made adequate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang urged the emperor to suspend nonessential work and cut wasteful spending to support the army, and the treasury was brought into balance.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，制建宗廟。

translations.literal: On gengchen an ordinance established the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen an ordinance established the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 太祖高皇帝，世祖光武皇帝，皆百世不遷。

translations.literal: Founding Ancestor Emperor Gao and Shizu Emperor Guangwu were both not to be removed for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Founding Ancestor Emperor Gao and Shizu Emperor Guangwu were both to remain in the temple for a hundred generations without removal.

sentences.zh: 又立四親廟，追尊謚號。

translations.literal: Four temples for close forebears were also established, with posthumous honorific titles conferred.
translations.idiomatic: Four temples for close forebears were also established and posthumous titles conferred.

sentences.zh: 凡六廟。

translations.literal: In all there were six temples.
translations.idiomatic: Six temples in all.

sentences.zh: 麻荅貪猾殘忍，民間有珍貨、美婦女，必奪取之。

translations.literal: Mada was greedy, cunning, and cruel; whenever the common people had rare goods or beautiful women, he was sure to seize them.
translations.idiomatic: Mada was greedy, cunning, and brutal. Whenever the people had rare goods or beautiful women, he seized them.

sentences.zh: 又捕村民，誣以為盜，披面，抉目，斷腕，焚炙而殺之，欲以威眾。

translations.literal: He also seized village people, falsely charged them as bandits, flayed their faces, gouged out their eyes, severed their wrists, burned and roasted them to death, wishing thereby to awe the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: He also seized villagers, falsely accused them of banditry, flayed their faces, gouged out their eyes, severed their wrists, and burned them alive to terrify the people.

sentences.zh: 常以其具自隨，左右前後懸人肝、膽、手、足，飲食起居於其間，語笑自若。

translations.literal: He constantly carried his implements with him; to left and right, before and behind, human livers, gall bladders, hands, and feet were hung; he ate, drank, rose, and rested among them, speaking and laughing as if at ease.
translations.idiomatic: He kept his tools with him always. Human livers, gall bladders, hands, and feet hung all around him as he ate, drank, and slept among them, talking and laughing as if nothing were amiss.

sentences.zh: 出入或被黃衣，用乘輿，服御物，曰：「茲事漢人以為不可，吾國無忌也。」

translations.literal: Going in and out he sometimes wore yellow robes, used the imperial carriage, and employed imperial regalia, saying, "In these matters the Han consider them impermissible—in our state there is no taboo."
translations.idiomatic: He sometimes went about in yellow robes, used the imperial carriage, and wore imperial regalia, saying, "The Han forbid such things—in our land there is no taboo."

sentences.zh: 又以宰相員不足，乃牒馮道判弘文館，李崧判史館，和凝判集賢，劉昫判中書，其僭妄如此。

translations.literal: Moreover, because the chief ministers were insufficient in number, he issued documents assigning Feng Dao to oversee the Hongwen Institute, Li Song the History Institute, He Ning the Jixian Institute, and Liu Xu the Secretariat—his presumption was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the chief ministers insufficient, he issued orders assigning Feng Dao to the Hongwen Institute, Li Song the History Institute, He Ning the Jixian Institute, and Liu Xu the Secretariat—such was his arrogance.

sentences.zh: 然契丹或犯法，無所容貸，故市肆不擾。

translations.literal: Yet when Khitan violated the law, there was no allowance whatsoever; therefore the markets were not disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Khitan broke the law, he showed no mercy, so the markets were not disturbed.

sentences.zh: 常恐漢人亡去，謂門者曰：「漢有窺門者，即斷其首以來。」

translations.literal: He constantly feared that Han people would flee; he told the gatekeepers, "If any Han is found peering at the gate, cut off his head and bring it here."
translations.idiomatic: He lived in constant fear that the Han would slip away. He told the gatekeepers, "If you see a Han spying at the gate, cut off his head and bring it to me."

sentences.zh: 麻荅遣使督運於洺州，洺州防禦使薛懷讓聞帝入大梁，殺其使者，舉州降。

translations.literal: Mada sent envoys to oversee transport at Mingzhou; Mingzhou defense commissioner Xue Huairang, hearing the Emperor had entered Daliang, killed the envoys and surrendered the entire prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Mada sent envoys to supervise transport at Mingzhou. When defense commissioner Xue Huairang learned the Emperor had entered Daliang, he killed the envoys and surrendered the whole prefecture.

sentences.zh: 帝遣郭從義將兵萬人會懷讓攻劉鐸於邢州，不克，鐸請兵於麻荅，麻荅遣其將楊安及前義武節度使李殷將千騎攻懷讓於洺州。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Guo Congyi leading ten thousand troops to join Huairang in attacking Liu Duo at Xingzhou; they did not take it; Duo requested troops from Mada; Mada sent his general Yang An and former Yiwu military governor Li Yin leading a thousand horsemen to attack Huairang at Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor dispatched Guo Congyi with ten thousand men to join Huairang in besieging Liu Duo at Xingzhou. The attack failed. Duo appealed to Mada, who sent his general Yang An and the former Yiwu military governor Li Yin with a thousand cavalry to strike Huairang at Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 懷讓嬰城自守，安等縱兵大掠於邢、洺之境。

translations.literal: Huairang shut the city and defended himself; An and the others let their troops rampage and plunder greatly in the territory of Xing and Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Huairang sealed the city and held out. Yang An and his fellows unleashed their troops to loot across Xing and Ming.

sentences.zh: 契丹所留兵不滿二千，麻荅令所司給萬四千人食，收其餘以自入。

translations.literal: The Khitan troops left behind numbered fewer than two thousand; Mada ordered the authorities to issue provisions for fourteen thousand men and pocketed the remainder himself.
translations.idiomatic: Fewer than two thousand Khitan remained on station. Mada ordered the supply offices to ration food for fourteen thousand men and kept the surplus for himself.

sentences.zh: 麻荅常疑漢兵，且以為無用，稍稍廢省，又損其食以飼胡兵。

translations.literal: Mada constantly distrusted the Han troops and moreover regarded them as useless; he gradually abolished and cut back units, and again reduced their rations to feed the barbarian troops.
translations.idiomatic: Mada never trusted the Han soldiers and deemed them worthless. He steadily pared their units and cut their rations to feed his own barbarian troops.

sentences.zh: 眾心怨憤，聞帝入大梁，皆有南歸之志。

translations.literal: Hearts were filled with resentment and anger; hearing the Emperor had entered Daliang, all cherished the wish to return south.
translations.idiomatic: Resentment ran deep. When word came that the Emperor had reached Daliang, every man yearned to go home to the south.

sentences.zh: 前穎州防禦使何福進，控鶴指揮使太原李榮，潛結軍中壯士數十人謀攻契丹，然畏契丹尚強，猶豫未發。

translations.literal: Former Yingzhou defense commissioner He Fujin and Crane Guard commander Li Rong of Taiyuan secretly joined several dozen stalwarts in the army to plot attacking the Khitan, yet fearing the Khitan were still strong, they hesitated and did not act.
translations.idiomatic: Former Yingzhou defense commissioner He Fujin and Crane Guard commander Li Rong of Taiyuan quietly rallied several dozen bold soldiers to plot a strike against the Khitan, but fearing the invaders were still too strong, they held back.

sentences.zh: 會楊袞、楊安等軍出，契丹留恆州者才八百人，福進等遂決計，約以擊佛寺鐘為號。

translations.literal: When Yang Gun, Yang An, and others marched out with their armies, only eight hundred Khitan remained at Hengzhou; Fujin and the others then resolved on their plan, agreeing to strike the Buddhist temple bell as the signal.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Gun and Yang An marched out, only eight hundred Khitan were left in Hengzhou. Fujin and his comrades settled on a plan: the temple bell would be their signal.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，契丹主兀欲遣騎至恆州，召前威勝節度使兼中書令馮道、樞密使李崧、左僕射和凝等，會葬契丹主德光於木葉山。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Khitan Emperor Wuyu sent horsemen to Hengzhou to summon former Weisheng military governor and concurrent Central Secretariat director Feng Dao, chief councillor Li Song, left vice director He Ning, and others to attend the burial of Khitan Emperor Deguang at Mount Muye.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, the Khitan emperor Wuyu sent cavalry to Hengzhou to summon Feng Dao, former Weisheng governor and concurrent director of the Central Secretariat, chief councillor Li Song, left vice director He Ning, and others to join the funeral of Emperor Deguang at Mount Muye.

sentences.zh: 道等未行，食時，鐘聲發。

translations.literal: Before Dao and the others had set out, at mealtime the bell sounded.
translations.idiomatic: Dao and his party had not yet departed when, at the hour of the meal, the bell rang out.

sentences.zh: 漢兵奪契丹守門者兵，擊契丹，殺十餘人，因突入府中。

translations.literal: Han soldiers seized the weapons of the Khitan gate guards, struck the Khitan, killed more than ten men, and thereupon burst into the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Han troops seized weapons from the Khitan gate guards, fell on the garrison, killed more than a dozen men, and stormed into the government compound.

sentences.zh: 李榮先據甲庫，悉召漢兵及市人，以鎧仗授之。

translations.literal: Li Rong first seized the armor storehouse, summoned all Han soldiers and townspeople, and issued them armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rong seized the armory first, called up every Han soldier and townsman he could find, and handed out armor and arms.

sentences.zh: 焚牙門，與契丹戰。

translations.literal: They burned the yamen gate and fought the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: They torched the main gate and battled the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 榮召諸將並力，護聖左廂都指揮使、恩州團練使白再榮狐疑，匿於別室，軍吏以佩刀決幕，引其臂，再榮不得已而行。

translations.literal: Rong called on the generals to unite their strength; Protector of the Realm left wing commander and Enzhou regiment commander Bai Zairong wavered and hid in another room; a staff officer cut through the curtain with his sword, took his arm, and Zairong went forth unwillingly.
translations.idiomatic: Rong rallied the generals to fight as one. Bai Zairong, commander of the Protector of the Realm left wing and Enzhou regiment commander, hung back and hid in a side room until a staff officer slashed through the curtain with his sword, seized his arm, and dragged him out.

sentences.zh: 諸將繼至，煙火四起，鼓噪震地。

translations.literal: The generals arrived in succession; smoke and fire rose on every side; the clamor of drums shook the ground.
translations.idiomatic: More generals hurried in. Smoke and flame leapt up everywhere; the roar of drums shook the earth.

sentences.zh: 麻荅等大驚，載寶貨家屬，走保北城。

translations.literal: Mada and the others were greatly alarmed; they loaded treasures and families and fled to hold the north city.
translations.idiomatic: Mada and his party panicked, loaded their valuables and families, and fled to the north quarter of the city.

sentences.zh: 而漢兵無所統壹，貪狡者乘亂剽掠，懦者竄匿。

translations.literal: But the Han troops had no unified command; the greedy and cunning plundered amid the chaos, and the timid hid themselves away.
translations.idiomatic: The Han forces had no single commander. The greedy looted in the confusion; the timid scattered and hid.

sentences.zh: 八月，壬午朔，契丹自北門入，勢復振，漢民死者二千餘人。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the first day renwu, Khitan entered from the north gate; their momentum revived; more than two thousand Han civilians died.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eighth month, renwu, Khitan poured in through the north gate and regained the upper hand. More than two thousand Han civilians were killed.

sentences.zh: 前磁州刺史李穀恐事不濟，請馮道、李崧、和凝至戰所慰勉士卒，士卒見道等至，爭自奮。

translations.literal: Former Cizhou prefect Li Gu, fearing affairs would not succeed, asked Feng Dao, Li Song, and He Ning to come to the battlefield to comfort and encourage the troops; when the soldiers saw Dao and the others arrive, they vied to rouse themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Former Cizhou prefect Li Gu, fearing defeat, brought Feng Dao, Li Song, and He Ning to the front to hearten the men. At the sight of them the troops rallied with fresh zeal.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，有村民數千噪於城外，欲奪契丹寶貨、婦女，契丹懼而北遁，麻荅、劉晞、崔廷勳皆奔定州，與義武節度使邪律忠合。

translations.literal: As dusk fell, several thousand villagers clamored outside the walls, wishing to seize Khitan treasures and women; the Khitan, afraid, fled north; Mada, Liu Xi, and Cui Tingxun all fled to Dingzhou and joined Yiwu military governor Yelü Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk thousands of villagers raised a clamor outside the walls, bent on Khitan loot and women. The Khitan, terrified, fled north. Mada, Liu Xi, and Cui Tingxun all ran to Dingzhou and joined Yiwu military governor Yelü Zhong.

sentences.zh: 忠，即郎五也。

translations.literal: Zhong was none other than Lang Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was none other than Lang Wu.

sentences.zh: 馮道等四出安撫兵民，眾推道為節度使。

translations.literal: Feng Dao and the others went out in four directions to pacify soldiers and people; the multitude urged Dao to become military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao and his colleagues fanned out to calm soldiers and civilians. The people pressed Dao to accept the post of military governor.

sentences.zh: 道曰：「我，書生也，當奏事而已，宜擇諸將為留後。」

translations.literal: Dao said, "I am but a scholar; I ought only to memorialize the throne; you should choose one of the generals as acting governor."
translations.idiomatic: Dao said, "I am only a scholar. My place is to report to the throne. Choose one of the generals as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 時李榮功最多，而白再榮位在上，乃以再榮權知留後，具以狀聞，且請援兵。

translations.literal: At the time Li Rong had achieved the most, but Bai Zairong outranked him; thus Zairong was made acting governor, the full circumstances were reported, and reinforcements were requested.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rong had done the most, but Bai Zairong outranked him, so Zairong was made acting governor. A full report went to the court, with a request for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 帝遣左飛龍使李彥從將兵赴之。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Left Flying Dragon commissioner Li Yancong leading troops to go to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Left Flying Dragon commissioner Li Yancong with an army to relieve them.

sentences.zh: 白再榮貪昧，猜忌諸將。

translations.literal: Bai Zairong was greedy and obtuse and suspicious of the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Zairong was greedy, dull, and suspicious of his fellow generals.

sentences.zh: 奉國廂主華池王饒恐為再榮所並，詐稱足疾，據東門樓，嚴兵自衛。

translations.literal: Nation-Serving Chamber chief Wang Rao of Huachi, fearing absorption by Zairong, falsely claimed foot ailment, held the east gate tower, and kept strict guard for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rao of Huachi, chief of the Nation-Serving Chamber, feared Zairong would swallow his command. He feigned a foot ailment, seized the east gate tower, and kept a tight guard.

sentences.zh: 司天監趙延乂善於二人，往來諭釋，始得解。

translations.literal: Director of Astronomy Zhao Yanyi was on good terms with both men; going back and forth he explained and reconciled them, and at last the standoff was resolved.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Astronomy Zhao Yanyi, who was friendly with both sides, shuttled between them until the quarrel was settled.

sentences.zh: 再榮以李崧、和凝久為相，家富，遣軍士圍其第求賞給，崧、凝各以家財與之，又欲殺崧、凝以滅口。

translations.literal: Zairong, because Li Song and He Ning had long served as chancellors and their households were wealthy, sent soldiers to surround their mansions demanding rewards; Song and Ning each gave their household wealth; he also wished to kill Song and Ning to silence them.
translations.idiomatic: Zairong knew Li Song and He Ning had long been chancellors and were rich. He sent troops to surround their mansions and demand payment. They paid from their own estates, yet he still meant to kill them to seal their lips.

sentences.zh: 李穀往見再榮，責之曰：「國亡主辱，公輩握兵不救。

translations.literal: Li Gu went to see Zairong and reproached him, saying, "The state perished and the ruler was shamed, yet you who held troops did not rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gu confronted Zairong. "The realm fell and the sovereign was disgraced," he said, "yet you who held armies did nothing to save him.

sentences.zh: 今僅能逐一虜將，鎮民死者近三千人，豈獨公之力邪！

translations.literal: Now you have barely managed to drive off one barbarian general; nearly three thousand people of the prefecture have died—is that solely your achievement?
translations.idiomatic: You have barely driven off one Khitan commander, and nearly three thousand townspeople are dead. Do you imagine that victory is yours alone?

sentences.zh: 才得脫死，遽欲殺宰相，新天子若詰公專殺之罪，公何辭以對？」

translations.literal: Having just escaped death, you rush to kill chancellors—if the new Son of Heaven questions you for unauthorized killing, what defense will you offer?"
translations.idiomatic: You have scarcely escaped with your life, and already you would murder chancellors. When the new emperor asks by what right you killed them, what answer will you give?"

sentences.zh: 再榮懼而止。

translations.literal: Zairong, afraid, desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Frightened, Zairong desisted.

sentences.zh: 又欲率民財以給軍，穀力爭之，乃止。

translations.literal: He also wished to levy the people's wealth to supply the army; Gu argued strenuously, and he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: He next tried to strip the people's wealth to pay the army. Gu fought him on it until he gave up.

sentences.zh: 漢人嘗事麻荅者，再榮皆拘之以取其財，恆人以其貪虐，謂之「白麻荅」。

translations.literal: Han who had once served Mada were all detained by Zairong to seize their wealth; the people of Heng, for his greed and cruelty, called him "White Mada."
translations.idiomatic: Every Han who had served under Mada, Zairong seized and robbed. The people of Heng, for his greed and cruelty, nicknamed him "White Mada."

sentences.zh: 楊袞至邢州，聞麻荅被逐，即日北還，楊安亦遁去，李殷以其眾來降。

translations.literal: Yang Gun reached Xingzhou; hearing Mada had been driven off, he returned north the same day; Yang An also fled; Li Yin brought his followers to surrender.
