translations.idiomatic: Yang Gun reached Xingzhou. Learning Mada had been driven out, he turned north the same day. Yang An fled as well, and Li Yin surrendered with his troops.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，以薛懷讓為安國節度使。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Xue Huairang was appointed Anguo military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Xue Huairang was appointed military governor of Anguo.

sentences.zh: 劉鐸聞麻荅遁去，舉邢州降；

translations.literal: Liu Duo, hearing Mada had fled, surrendered Xingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Duo heard Mada had fled, he surrendered Xingzhou;

sentences.zh: 懷讓詐云巡檢，引兵向邢州，鐸開門納之，懷讓殺鐸，以克復聞。

translations.literal: Huairang falsely claimed to be on inspection, led troops toward Xingzhou; Duo opened the gates and admitted them; Huairang killed Duo and reported the recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Huairang pretended he was merely inspecting the circuit and marched on Xingzhou. Duo opened the gates to admit him. Huairang killed Duo and reported a reconquest.

sentences.zh: 朝廷知而不問。

translations.literal: The court knew of it but made no inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The court knew what had happened but asked no questions.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，復以恆州順國軍為鎮州成德軍。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Hengzhou's Shunguo Army was again made Zhenzhou's Chengde Army.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, the Shunguo Army of Hengzhou was restored as the Chengde Army of Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 乙未，以白再榮為成德留後。

translations.literal: On yiwei, Bai Zairong was made Chengde acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Bai Zairong was appointed acting governor of Chengde.

sentences.zh: 逾年，始以何福進為曹州防禦使，李榮為博州刺史。

translations.literal: More than a year later, He Fujin was at last made Caozhou defense commissioner and Li Rong Bozhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Only after more than a year was He Fujin made defense commissioner of Caozhou and Li Rong prefect of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 敕：「盜賊毋問贓多少皆抵死。」

translations.literal: An edict: "For bandits, regardless of how much booty is involved, all shall suffer death."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Bandits shall be put to death, no matter how small the loot.

sentences.zh: 時四方盜賊多，朝廷患之，故重其法，仍分命使者逐捕。

translations.literal: At the time bandits were numerous everywhere; the court was troubled and therefore stiffened the law, also dispatching envoys in separate assignments to hunt them down.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were rampant throughout the realm, and the court, alarmed, tightened the law and sent out commissioners to hunt them down.

sentences.zh: 蘇逢吉自草詔，意云：「應賊盜，並四鄰同保，皆全族處斬。」

translations.literal: Su Fengji himself drafted the edict, meaning: "Wherever bandits appear, the four neighboring households in mutual guarantee shall all be executed, entire clans put to death."
translations.idiomatic: Su Fengji drafted the edict himself. His wording called for every bandit and the four neighboring households under mutual guarantee to be executed, entire clans included.

sentences.zh: 眾以為：「盜猶不可族，況鄰保乎！」

translations.literal: The multitude said, "Even for bandits clans cannot be extinguished—how much less for mutual-guarantee neighbors!"
translations.idiomatic: Others objected: "You cannot wipe out a clan even for theft—how much less the neighbors who vouch for them!

sentences.zh: 逢吉固爭，不得已，但省去「全族」字。

translations.literal: Fengji obstinately argued; with no alternative, only the words "entire clans" were removed.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji dug in his heels. In the end only the phrase "entire clans" was struck out.

sentences.zh: 由是捕賊使者張令柔殺平陰十七村民。

translations.literal: "Thereupon the bandit-hunting envoy Zhang Lingrou killed seventeen villagers of Pingyin."
translations.idiomatic: "On that authority the bandit-hunting envoy Zhang Lingrou executed seventeen villagers of Pingyin."

sentences.zh: 逢吉為人，文深好殺。

translations.literal: Fengji as a man was steeped in harshness and fond of killing.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji was harsh by nature and bloodthirsty.

sentences.zh: 在河東幕府，帝嘗令靜獄以祈福，逢吉盡殺獄囚還報。

translations.literal: In the Hedong headquarters, the Emperor once ordered quieting of the prisons to seek blessings; Fengji killed all prisoners in the jails and returned with his report.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in the Hedong headquarters, the Emperor once ordered the prisons cleared to bring peace and good fortune. Fengji executed every prisoner and reported the task done.

sentences.zh: 及為相，朝廷草創，帝悉以軍旅之事委楊邠、郭威，百司庶務委逢吉及蘇禹珪。

translations.literal: When he became chancellor, the court was newly founded; the Emperor wholly entrusted military affairs to Yang Bin and Guo Wei, and the hundred offices' routine business to Fengji and Su Yugui.
translations.idiomatic: Once he was chancellor, with the court still taking shape, the Emperor left all military affairs to Yang Bin and Guo Wei and the daily business of government to Fengji and Su Yugui.

sentences.zh: 二相決事，皆出胸臆，不拘舊制。

translations.literal: The two chancellors decided affairs all from their own breasts, not bound by old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The two chancellors ruled from impulse, heedless of precedent.

sentences.zh: 雖事無留滯，而用捨黜陟，惟其所欲。

translations.literal: Though matters met no delay, appointments, dismissals, promotions, and demotions followed only their wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Business moved swiftly, but appointments and dismissals followed their whim alone.

sentences.zh: 帝方倚信之，無敢言者。

translations.literal: The Emperor was then relying on and trusting them; none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor trusted them utterly, and no one dared object.

sentences.zh: 逢吉尤貪詐，公求貨財，無所顧避。

translations.literal: Fengji was especially greedy and deceitful; accepting goods openly, he showed no scruple whatsoever.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji was greedier and more deceitful than any of them, taking bribes openly without a qualm.

sentences.zh: 繼母死，不為服；

translations.literal: When his stepmother died, he did not observe mourning;
translations.idiomatic: When his stepmother died, he refused mourning;

sentences.zh: 庶兄自外至，不白逢吉而見諸子，逢吉怒，密語郭威，以他事杖殺之。

translations.literal: a younger brother by another mother came from outside; without informing Fengji he visited the sons; Fengji was enraged, spoke secretly to Guo Wei, and had him clubbed to death on another charge.
translations.idiomatic: his half-brother arrived from abroad and visited the sons without telling Fengji. Enraged, Fengji whispered to Guo Wei, who had the man beaten to death on a pretext.

sentences.zh: 楚王希廣庶弟天策左司馬希崇，性狡險，陰遺兄希萼書，言劉彥□等違先王之命，廢長立少，以激怒之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Chu's younger brother by a concubine, Left Master of Strategy Xichong, was crafty and dangerous; he secretly sent elder brother Xie a letter, saying Liu Yan□ and others had violated the late king's command, deposing the elder to install the younger, to enrage him.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xiguang's younger brother Xichong, Left Master of Strategy, was sly and treacherous. He secretly wrote to his elder brother Xie that Liu Yan and others had defied their father's will by deposing the elder son to seat the younger, hoping to enrage him.

sentences.zh: 希萼自永州來奔喪，乙巳，至趺石，彥□白希廣遣侍從都指揮使周廷誨等將水軍逆之，命永州將士皆釋甲而入，館希萼於碧湘宮，成服於其次，不聽入與希廣相見。

translations.literal: Xie came from Yongzhou to attend the funeral; on yiwei he reached Dieshi; Yan□ reported to Xiguang, who dispatched attendant commander Zhou Tinghui and others with the navy to meet him, ordered Yongzhou officers and soldiers to lay down armor before entering, lodged Xie at Bixiang Palace, observed mourning at a separate site, and did not allow him to enter and see Xiguang.
translations.idiomatic: Xie came from Yongzhou for the funeral. On yiwei he reached Dieshi. Liu Yan informed Xiguang, who sent attendant commander Zhou Tinghui with the fleet to meet him, ordered the Yongzhou troops to enter unarmed, lodged Xie at Bixiang Palace, and made him mourn at a separate hall, forbidding any meeting with Xiguang.

sentences.zh: 希萼求示還朗州，周廷誨勸希廣殺之。

translations.literal: Xie asked permission to return to Langzhou; Zhou Tinghui urged Xiguang to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Xie asked leave to return to Langzhou. Zhou Tinghui urged Xiguang to kill him.

sentences.zh: 希廣曰：「吾何忍殺兄！

translations.literal: Xiguang said, "How could I bear to kill my brother!
translations.idiomatic: Xiguang said, "How could I bear to kill my own brother!

sentences.zh: 寧分潭、朗而治之。」

translations.literal: Better to divide Tan and Lang and each rule his own."
translations.idiomatic: Let us rather divide Tan and Lang and each rule his own.

sentences.zh: 乃厚贈希萼，遣還朗州。

translations.literal: He then lavished gifts on Xie and sent him back to Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Xie back to Langzhou with rich gifts.

sentences.zh: 希崇常為希萼詗希廣，語言動作，悉以告之，約為內應。

translations.literal: Xichong constantly spied on Xiguang for Xie; his words and movements were all reported, and they agreed he would serve as inside contact."
translations.idiomatic: Xichong constantly spied on Xiguang for Xie, reporting his every word and deed, and pledged to act as his inside man."

sentences.zh: 契丹之滅晉也，驅戰馬二萬匹歸其國。

translations.literal: When the Khitan destroyed Jin, they drove twenty thousand war horses back to their state.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan destroyed Jin, they drove twenty thousand war horses home.

sentences.zh: 至是漢兵乏馬，詔市士民馬於河南諸道不經剽掠者。

translations.literal: At this time Han troops lacked horses; an edict ordered purchasing civilian horses from the Henan circuits that had not suffered plundering.
translations.idiomatic: Now Han armies were short of horses. An edict ordered buying horses from civilians in the Henan circuits that had escaped the worst looting.

sentences.zh: 制以錢弘倧為東南兵馬都元帥、鎮海、鎮東節度使兼中書令、吳越王。

translations.literal: By decree Qian Hongzuo was made Southeast military commander-in-chief, Zhenhai and Zhendong military governor, concurrent Central Secretariat director, and King of Wuyue.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial decree Qian Hongzuo was named Southeast commander-in-chief, military governor of Zhenhai and Zhendong, concurrent director of the Central Secretariat, and King of Wuyue.

sentences.zh: 高從誨聞杜重威叛，發水軍數千襲襄州，山南東道節度使安審琦擊卻之。

translations.literal: Gao Conghui, hearing Du Chongwei had rebelled, launched several thousand naval troops to raid Xiangzhou; Shannan East Circuit military governor An Shenqi repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Conghui, hearing Du Chongwei had rebelled, sent several thousand naval troops against Xiangzhou. Shannan East Circuit military governor An Shenqi drove them off.

sentences.zh: 又寇郢州，刺史尹實大破之。

translations.literal: He again raided Yingzhou; prefect Yin Shi inflicted a great defeat on him.
translations.idiomatic: He raided Yingzhou next and was routed by prefect Yin Shi.

sentences.zh: 乃絕漢，附於唐、蜀。

translations.literal: He then broke with Han and attached himself to Tang and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He then broke with Han and turned to Tang and Shu.

sentences.zh: 初，荊南介居湖南、嶺南、福建之間，地狹兵弱，自武信王季興時，諸道入貢過其境者，多掠奪其貨幣。

translations.literal: Initially, Jingnan lay between Hunan, Lingnan, and Fujian—narrow territory, weak troops; since the time of Prince of Wuxin Ji Xing, tribute missions from various circuits passing through its territory often had their goods and currency plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Jingnan sat between Hunan, Lingnan, and Fujian—small territory, few troops. Ever since the days of Prince of Wuxin Ji Xing, envoys bearing tribute through its lands were often robbed of their goods.

sentences.zh: 及諸道移書詰讓，或加以兵，不得已復歸之，曾不為愧。

translations.literal: When circuits sent letters of censure, or added troops, they were forced to return the goods—yet felt no shame.
translations.idiomatic: When neighboring circuits protested in writing or threatened force, they returned the loot—yet felt no shame.

sentences.zh: 及從誨立，唐、晉、契丹、漢更據中原，南漢、閩、吳、蜀皆稱帝。

translations.literal: When Conghui came to power, Tang, Jin, Khitan, and Han in turn held the Central Plains; Southern Han, Min, Wu, and Shu all styled themselves emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Under Conghui, Tang, Jin, Khitan, and Han succeeded one another in the Central Plains while Southern Han, Min, Wu, and Shu each claimed the title of emperor.

sentences.zh: 從誨利其賜予，所向稱臣，諸國賤之，謂之「高無賴」。

translations.literal: Conghui coveted their gifts and bowed in every direction; the states despised him and called him "Gao the Shameless."
translations.idiomatic: Conghui craved their gifts and bowed to whoever would pay him. The other states despised him and called him "Gao the Shameless."

sentences.zh: 唐主以太傅兼中書令宋齊丘為鎮南節度使。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler appointed Grand Tutor and concurrent Central Secretariat director Song Qiqiu military governor of Zhennan.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang emperor appointed Grand Tutor and concurrent director of the Central Secretariat Song Qiqiu military governor of Zhennan.

sentences.zh: 南漢主恐諸弟與其子爭國，殺齊王弘弼、貴王弘道、定王弘益、辨王弘濟、同王弘簡、益王弘建、恩王弘偉、宜王弘照，盡殺其男，納其女充後宮。

translations.literal: The Southern Han ruler, fearing his younger brothers would contend for the realm with his son, killed Princes of Qi Hongbi, Gui Hongdao, Ding Hongyi, Bian Hongji, Tong Hongjian, Yi Hongjian, En Hongwei, and Yi Hongzhao, executed all their sons, and took their daughters into the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Han ruler, fearing his brothers would rival his son for the throne, executed Princes Hongbi of Qi, Hongdao of Gui, Hongyi of Ding, Hongji of Bian, Hongjian of Tong, Hongjian of Yi, Hongwei of En, and Hongzhao of Yi, killed all their sons, and took their daughters into the palace.

sentences.zh: 作離宮千餘間，飾以珠寶，設鑊湯、鐵床、刳剔等刑，號「生地獄」。

translations.literal: He built more than a thousand detached palaces, adorned with jewels, and set up punishments of boiling cauldrons, iron beds, disemboweling and flaying—called the "Hell of the Living."
translations.idiomatic: He built more than a thousand pleasure palaces studded with gems and equipped them with boiling cauldrons, iron beds, disemboweling, and flaying—the whole apparatus nicknamed the Hell of the Living.

sentences.zh: 嘗醉，戲以瓜置樂工之頸試劍，遂斷其頭。

translations.literal: Once drunk, he playfully placed a melon on a musician's neck to test his sword and severed his head.
translations.idiomatic: Once, drunk, he set a melon on a musician's neck to try his sword and cut off the man's head.

sentences.zh: 初，帝與吏部尚書竇貞固俱事晉高祖，雅相知重，及即位，欲以為相，問蘇逢吉：「其次誰可相者？」

translations.literal: Initially, the Emperor and Minister of Personnel Dou Zhengu had both served Jin Gaozu and held each other in esteem; on taking the throne he wished to make Zhengu chancellor and asked Su Fengji, "Who next could serve as chancellor?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Emperor and Minister of Personnel Dou Zhengu had both served under Jin Gaozu and respected each other. On his accession he meant to make Zhengu chancellor and asked Su Fengji, "Who else could serve as chancellor?"

sentences.zh: 逢吉與翰林學士李濤善，因薦之，曰：「昔濤乞斬張彥譯，陛下在太原，嘗重之，此可相也。」

translations.literal: Fengji was friendly with Hanlin academician Li Tao and therefore recommended him, saying, "Formerly Tao petitioned to execute Zhang Yanze; Your Majesty at Taiyuan once valued him—he can be chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: Fengji was close to Hanlin academician Li Tao and recommended him: "Tao once asked that Zhang Yanze be executed. Your Majesty valued him at Taiyuan. He is fit for the post."

sentences.zh: 會高行周、慕容彥超共討杜重威於鄴都，彥超欲急攻城，行周欲緩之以待其弊。

translations.literal: It happened that Gao Xingzhou and Murong Yanchao were jointly attacking Du Chongwei at Yedu; Yanchao wished to press the siege, Xingzhou wished to delay to wait for their exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Gao Xingzhou and Murong Yanchao were besieging Du Chongwei at Yedu. Yanchao wanted a swift assault; Xingzhou preferred to wait until hunger broke the city.

sentences.zh: 行周女為重威子婦，彥超揚言：「行周以女故，愛賊不攻。」

translations.literal: Xingzhou's daughter was Chongwei's son's wife; Yanchao proclaimed aloud, "Xingzhou, for his daughter's sake, loves the bandit and will not attack."
translations.idiomatic: Xingzhou's daughter was married to Chongwei's son. Yanchao spread the word that Xingzhou spared the rebel because of family ties.

sentences.zh: 由是二將不協。

translations.literal: From this the two generals were at odds.
translations.idiomatic: From that day the two generals were at odds.

sentences.zh: 帝恐生他變，欲自將擊重威，意未決。

translations.literal: The Emperor feared other changes would arise and wished to lead the attack on Chongwei himself, but his mind was not settled.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor feared further trouble and thought of leading the campaign himself, but could not decide.

sentences.zh: 濤上疏請親征。

translations.literal: Tao memorialized requesting a personal campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tao memorialized urging the Emperor to take the field in person.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，以濤有宰相器。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and deemed Tao possessed the makings of a chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was delighted and judged Tao to have the makings of a chancellor.

sentences.zh: 九月，甲戌，加逢吉左僕射兼門下侍郎，蘇禹珪右僕射兼中書侍郎，貞固司空兼門下侍郎，濤戶部尚書兼中書侍郎，並同平章事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on jiaxu, Fengji was advanced to left vice director and concurrent Gate head; Yugui to right vice director and concurrent Secretariat vice head; Zhengu to minister of works and concurrent Gate vice head; Tao to minister of revenue and concurrent Secretariat vice head—all concurrent chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jiaxu, Fengji was made left vice director and concurrent vice head of the Gate Department; Yugui right vice director and concurrent vice head of the Secretariat; Zhengu minister of works and concurrent vice head of the Gate Department; Tao minister of revenue and concurrent vice head of the Secretariat—all as chief ministers of state.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，詔幸澶、魏勞軍，以皇子承訓為東京留守。

translations.literal: "On wuyin, an edict ordered visiting Chan and Wei to encourage the troops, with Prince Chengxun as Eastern Capital regent."
translations.idiomatic: "On wuyin an edict ordered the Emperor to visit Chan and Wei to hearten the armies, with Prince Chengxun left as regent of the Eastern Capital."

sentences.zh: 馮道、李崧、和凝自鎮州還。

translations.literal: Feng Dao, Li Song, and He Ning returned from Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao, Li Song, and He Ning returned from Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 己卯，以崧為太子太傅，凝為太子太保。

translations.literal: On jimao, Song was made Crown Prince Grand Tutor and He Ning Crown Prince Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Li Song was made Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince and He Ning Grand Guardian of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，帝發大梁。

translations.literal: On gengchen, the Emperor set out from Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen the Emperor departed Daliang.

sentences.zh: 晉昌節度使趙匡贊恐終不為朝廷所容，冬，十月，遣使降蜀，請自終南山路出兵應援。

translations.literal: Jinchang military governor Zhao Kuangzan, fearing he would never be tolerated by the court, in winter, the tenth month, sent envoys to surrender to Shu, asking to march out by the Zhongnan Mountain route in support.
translations.idiomatic: Jinchang military governor Zhao Kuangzan, fearing the court would never trust him, sent envoys in the tenth month of winter to surrender to Shu and offered to march through the Zhongnan Mountains in support.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，帝至鄴都城下，捨於高行周營。

translations.literal: On wuxu, the Emperor reached below the walls of Yedu and lodged in Gao Xingzhou's camp.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu the Emperor reached Yedu and took quarters in Gao Xingzhou's camp.

sentences.zh: 行周言於帝曰：「城中食未盡，急攻，徒殺士卒，未易克也。

translations.literal: Xingzhou said to the Emperor, "Provisions in the city are not yet exhausted; pressing the attack will only waste soldiers' lives and will not be easy to take.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzhou told the Emperor, "Their food has not run out. A hasty assault will only waste our men and still fail to take the city.

sentences.zh: 不若緩之，彼食盡自潰。」

translations.literal: Better to delay; when their food is gone they will collapse of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Wait them out. When their stores are gone they will fall apart on their own.

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The Emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 慕容彥超數因事陵轢行周，行周泣訴於執政，掏糞壤實其口，蘇逢吉、楊邠密以白帝。

translations.literal: Murong Yanchao repeatedly used occasions to insult and bully Xingzhou; Xingzhou wept and complained to the chief ministers, dug up dung and earth and stuffed it in his own mouth; Su Fengji and Yang Bin secretly reported this to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yanchao repeatedly humiliated Xingzhou on one pretext or another. Xingzhou wept before the chief ministers, scooped up dung and earth, and stuffed it into his own mouth. Su Fengji and Yang Bin quietly informed the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝深知彥超之曲，猶命二臣和解之。

translations.literal: The Emperor deeply knew Yanchao was in the wrong, yet still ordered the two ministers to reconcile them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor knew full well that Yanchao was in the wrong, yet he still ordered the two chief ministers to patch things up between them.

sentences.zh: 又召彥超於帳中責之，且使詣行周謝。

translations.literal: He also summoned Yanchao into the tent to rebuke him, and moreover made him go to Xingzhou to apologize."
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned Yanchao into his tent, rebuked him, and sent him to apologize to Xingzhou."

sentences.zh: 杜重威聲言車駕至即降，帝遣給事中陳觀往諭指，重威復閉門拒之。

translations.literal: Du Chongwei publicly declared that when the imperial carriage arrived he would surrender; the Emperor sent Supervising Secretary Chen Guan to convey his intent, but Chongwei again shut the gates and refused him.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chongwei had announced that he would surrender as soon as the Emperor arrived. The Emperor sent Supervising Secretary Chen Guan to deliver his terms, but Chongwei shut the gates and turned him away again.

sentences.zh: 城中食浸竭，將士多出降者。

translations.literal: Food in the city gradually ran out, and many officers and soldiers came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: As provisions in the city dwindled, more and more officers and soldiers slipped out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 慕容彥超固請攻城，帝從之。

translations.literal: Murong Yanchao firmly pressed to assault the city, and the Emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yanchao pressed hard for an assault, and the Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 丙午，親督諸將攻城，自寅至辰，士卒傷者萬餘人，死者千餘人，不克而止。

translations.literal: On bingwu, he personally directed the generals in storming the city; from yin to chen, more than ten thousand soldiers were wounded and more than a thousand killed, and they stopped without taking it.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu the Emperor personally directed the generals in an assault. From the yin hour through chen, more than ten thousand men were wounded and over a thousand killed. The attack failed and was called off.

sentences.zh: 彥超乃不敢復言。

translations.literal: Yanchao then dared speak no more.
translations.idiomatic: After that Yanchao did not dare raise the matter again.

sentences.zh: 初，契丹留幽州兵千五百人戍大梁。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Khitan had left fifteen hundred Youzhou troops to garrison Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Khitan had left fifteen hundred Youzhou troops to garrison Daliang.

sentences.zh: 帝入大梁，或告幽州兵將為變，帝盡殺之於繁台之下。

translations.literal: When the Emperor entered Daliang, someone reported that the Youzhou troops were about to mutiny, and the Emperor had them all killed below Fantai.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor entered Daliang, someone warned that the Youzhou garrison was plotting mutiny. He had every one of them slaughtered below Fantai.

sentences.zh: 乃圍鄴都，張璉將幽州兵二千助重威拒守，帝屢遣人招諭，許以不死。

translations.literal: Then he besieged Yedu; Zhang Lian led two thousand Youzhou troops to help Chongwei hold out, and the Emperor repeatedly sent men to summon and instruct them, promising they would not be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: He then laid siege to Yedu. Zhang Lian led two thousand Youzhou troops to help Chongwei hold the city. The Emperor sent envoys again and again, promising that anyone who submitted would be spared.

sentences.zh: 璉曰：「繁台之卒，何罪而戮？

translations.literal: Lian said, "The soldiers at Fantai—what crime had they committed to be slaughtered?
translations.idiomatic: Lian said, "What crime had the men at Fantai committed, that they were slaughtered?

sentences.zh: 今守此，以死為期耳。」

translations.literal: Now we hold this place with death as our term."
translations.idiomatic: We hold this city now only to die in it.

sentences.zh: 由是城久不下。

translations.literal: For this reason the city long would not fall.
translations.idiomatic: For that reason the city held out for a long time.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丙辰，內殿直韓訓獻攻城之具，帝曰：「城之所恃者，眾心耳。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on bingchen, Inner Palace Guard Han Xun presented siege equipment; the Emperor said, "What a city relies on is the hearts of the multitude alone.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on bingchen, Inner Palace Guard Han Xun presented siege engines. The Emperor said, "A city stands only on the loyalty of its people.

sentences.zh: 眾心苟離，城無所保，用此何為！」

translations.literal: If the multitude's hearts depart, the city has nothing to preserve—what use is this!"
translations.idiomatic: Once those hearts are gone, no wall can save it. What good are engines then?"

sentences.zh: 杜重威之叛，觀察判官金鄉王敏屢泣諫，不聽。

translations.literal: At Du Chongwei's rebellion, Observation Commissioner aide Wang Min of Jinxiang repeatedly wept and remonstrated, but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Chongwei rebelled, Wang Min of Jinxiang, aide to the Observation Commissioner, pleaded with tears again and again, but Chongwei would not listen.

sentences.zh: 及食竭力盡，甲戌，遣敏奉表出降。

translations.literal: When food and strength were exhausted, on jiaxu he sent Min to present a memorial and come out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When food and strength were spent, on jiaxu he sent Min out with a surrender memorial.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，重威子弘璉來見；

translations.literal: On yihai, Chongwei's son Hong Lian came to an audience;
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Chongwei's son Hong Lian was received in audience;

sentences.zh: 丙子，妻石氏來見。

translations.literal: on bingzi, his wife the Lady Shi came to an audience.
translations.idiomatic: on bingzi his wife Lady Shi was received as well.

sentences.zh: 石氏，即晉之宋國長公主也，帝復遣入城。

translations.literal: The Lady Shi was none other than Jin's Princess of Song, and the Emperor sent her back into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Shi was the Jin dynasty's Princess of Song. The Emperor sent her back into the city.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，重威開門出降，城中餒死者什七八，存者皆尪瘠無人狀。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Chongwei opened the gates and came out to surrender; seven or eight tenths in the city had died of starvation, and the survivors were all wasted and emaciated beyond human likeness.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Chongwei opened the gates and surrendered. Seven or eight people in ten inside the city had starved to death; the survivors were so wasted and gaunt they scarcely looked human.

sentences.zh: 張璉先邀朝廷信誓，詔許以歸鄉里。

translations.literal: Zhang Lian first sought a sworn pledge from the court, and an edict promised he might return to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lian had first demanded a sworn pledge from the court, and an edict promised that he and his men could go home.

sentences.zh: 及出降，殺璉等將校數十人，縱其士卒北歸。

translations.literal: When they came out to surrender, he killed Lian and several dozen other officers, and released their soldiers to return north.
translations.idiomatic: Once they surrendered, he executed Lian and several dozen other officers, then let the rank and file march north.

sentences.zh: 將出境，大掠而去。

translations.literal: As they were about to leave the border, they plundered on a great scale and departed.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home they looted the countryside as they went.

sentences.zh: 郭威請殺重威牙將百餘人，並重威家貲籍之以賞戰士，從之。

translations.literal: Guo Wei requested killing more than a hundred of Chongwei's staff officers, and together with Chongwei's household wealth registering it to reward the warriors; this was followed.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei asked that more than a hundred of Chongwei's staff officers be executed and Chongwei's entire estate seized and distributed among the troops. The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 以重威為太傅兼中書令、楚國公。

translations.literal: Chongwei was made Grand Tutor and concurrently Director of the Secretariat, Duke of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Chongwei was appointed Grand Tutor, Director of the Secretariat, and Duke of Chu.

sentences.zh: 重威每出入，路人往往擲瓦礫詬之。

translations.literal: Whenever Chongwei went out or in, people on the road often threw tiles and stones and cursed him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Chongwei appeared in public, passersby pelted him with rubble and cursed him to his face.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：漢高祖殺幽州無辜千五百人，非仁也；

translations.literal: Your subject Guang says: Han Gaozu killed fifteen hundred innocent Youzhou men—this was not benevolence;
translations.idiomatic: Guang remarks: Gaozu of Han slaughtered fifteen hundred innocent Youzhou troops. That was not benevolence.

sentences.zh: 誘張璉而誅之，非信也；

translations.literal: he lured Zhang Lian and executed him—this was not faithfulness;
translations.idiomatic: He lured Zhang Lian in and put him to death. That was not good faith.

sentences.zh: 杜重威罪大而赦之，非刑也。

translations.literal: Du Chongwei's crime was great yet he pardoned him—this was not punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chongwei's crime was grave, yet he spared him. That was not justice.

sentences.zh: 仁以合眾，信以行令，刑以懲奸，失此三者，何以守國！

translations.literal: Benevolence is what binds the multitude, faithfulness is what carries out orders, punishment is what chastises the wicked—lose these three, and with what shall one keep a state!
translations.idiomatic: Benevolence binds the people together, faithfulness makes commands obeyed, and punishment restrains the wicked. Lose all three, and how can a state endure?

sentences.zh: 其祚運之不延也，宜哉！

translations.literal: That his fortune and mandate did not extend—how fitting!
translations.idiomatic: Small wonder that his dynasty did not last.

sentences.zh: 高行周以慕容彥超在澶州，固辭鄴都。

translations.literal: Gao Xingzhou, because Murong Yanchao was at Chanzou, firmly declined Yedu.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xingzhou firmly declined the post at Yedu while Murong Yanchao remained at Chanzou.

sentences.zh: 己卯，以忠武節度使史弘肇領歸德節度使，兼侍衛馬步都指揮使，義成節度使劉信領忠武節度使兼侍衛馬步副都指揮使，徙彥超為天平節度使，並加同平章事。

translations.literal: On jimao, Zhongwu military governor Shi Hongzhao was made to hold Guidde military governorship and concurrently Grand Commander of the Palace Horse and Foot Guards; Yicheng military governor Liu Xin was made to hold Zhongwu military governorship and concurrently Vice Grand Commander of the Palace Horse and Foot Guards; Yanchao was transferred to be Taiping military governor; all were additionally made Grand Councillors.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Shi Hongzhao, military governor of Zhongwu, was also made military governor of Guidde and Grand Commander of the Palace Horse and Foot Guards. Liu Xin, military governor of Yicheng, took over Zhongwu and became Vice Grand Commander of the Palace Horse and Foot Guards. Yanchao was transferred to Taiping. All three were promoted to Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 吳越王弘倧大閱水軍，賞賜倍於舊。

translations.literal: Wuyue King Hong Zong held a great review of the naval forces, with rewards double the former amount.
translations.idiomatic: King Hong Zong of Wuyue held a grand naval review and doubled the usual rewards.

sentences.zh: 胡進思固諫，弘倧怒，投筆水中，曰：「吾之財與士卒共之，奚多少之限邪！」

translations.literal: Hu Jinsi firmly remonstrated; Hong Zong grew angry, threw his brush into the water, and said, "My wealth I share with the soldiers—what limit of more or less is there!"
translations.idiomatic: Hu Jinsi protested firmly. Hong Zong flared up, flung his brush into the water, and said, "My wealth belongs to my men as much as to me. Why quibble over the amount?"

sentences.zh: 十二月，丙戌，帝發鄴都。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on bingxu, the Emperor set out from Yedu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on bingxu, the Emperor departed Yedu.

sentences.zh: 蜀主遣雄武都押牙吳崇惲，以樞密使王處回書招鳳翔節度使侯益。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler sent Xiongwu commandery adjutant Wu Chongyun, with a letter from Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner Wang Chuhui, to recruit Fengxiang military governor Hou Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Shu sent Wu Chongyun, adjutant of the Xiongwu command, with a letter from Wang Chuhui of the Bureau of Military Affairs to win over Hou Yi, military governor of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，以山南西道節度使兼中書令張虔釗為北面行營招討安撫使，雄武節度使何重建副之，宣徽使韓保貞為都虞候，共將兵五萬，虔釗出散關，重建出隴州，以擊鳳翔。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Shannan West Circuit military governor and concurrently Director of the Secretariat Zhang Qianzhao was made northern campaign Pacification and Reassurance Commissioner; Xiongwu military governor He Chongjian was his deputy; Palace Secretariat commissioner Han Baozhen was chief inspector; together they led fifty thousand troops—Qianzhao out by Sanguan Pass, Chongjian out by Longzhou—to strike Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Zhang Qianzhao, military governor of Shannan West Circuit and Director of the Secretariat, was appointed northern campaign Pacification Commissioner, with He Chongjian of Xiongwu as his deputy and Han Baozhen of the Palace Secretariat as chief inspector. They took fifty thousand men—Qianzhao through Sanguan Pass, Chongjian through Longzhou—to attack Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 奉鑾肅衛都虞候李廷珪將兵二萬出子午谷，以援長安。

translations.literal: Fengluan Imperial Guard chief inspector Li Tinggui led twenty thousand troops out through Ziwu Valley to relieve Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tinggui, chief inspector of the Imperial Guard, marched twenty thousand men through Ziwu Valley to relieve Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 諸軍發成都，旌旗數十里。

translations.literal: The various armies set out from Chengdu, their banners and flags stretching for several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: The armies left Chengdu with banners and flags stretching for miles.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，皇子開封尹承訓卒。

translations.literal: On xinmao, the Prince, Kaifeng Intendant Cheng Xun, died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Prince Cheng Xun, Intendant of Kaifeng, died.

sentences.zh: 承訓孝友忠厚，達於從政，人皆惜之。

translations.literal: Cheng Xun was filial, friendly, honest and generous, and accomplished in administration; all mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xun was filial, loyal to his friends, honest and generous, and skilled in government. All who knew him grieved.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，帝至大梁。

translations.literal: On guisi, the Emperor reached Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi the Emperor reached Daliang.

sentences.zh: 威武節度使李孺贇與吳越戍將鮑修讓不協，謀襲殺修讓，復以福州降唐。

translations.literal: Weiwu military governor Li Ruyin was at odds with Wuyue garrison general Bao Xiurang, plotted a surprise attack to kill Xiurang, and again offered Fuzhou in surrender to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruyin, military governor of Weiwu, fell out with Bao Xiurang, the Wuyue garrison commander, and plotted to kill him in a surprise attack and surrender Fuzhou to Tang once more.

sentences.zh: 修讓覺之，引兵攻府第，是日，殺孺贇，夷其族。

translations.literal: Xiurang detected it, led troops to attack the prefectural residence, and that day killed Ruyin and exterminated his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiurang learned of the plot, marched on the governor's residence, killed Ruyin that same day, and wiped out his entire clan.

sentences.zh: 乙未，追立皇子承訓為魏王。

translations.literal: On yiwei, posthumously established the Prince Cheng Xun as Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei the late Prince Cheng Xun was posthumously created Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 侯益請降於蜀，使吳崇惲持兵籍、糧帳西還，與趙匡贊同上表請出兵平定關中。

translations.literal: Hou Yi requested to surrender to Shu, sent Wu Chongyun west bearing military registers and grain accounts, and together with Zhao Kuangzan submitted a memorial asking to march out troops to pacify Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Yi offered to surrender to Shu. He sent Wu Chongyun west with the muster rolls and grain accounts and, together with Zhao Kuangzan, memorialized the Shu court to send an army to pacify Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 己酉，鮑修讓傳李孺贇首至錢塘，吳越王弘倧以丞相山陰吳程知威武節度事。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Bao Xiurang sent Li Ruyin's head to Qiantang; Wuyue King Hong Zong made Shanyin chief minister Wu Cheng administrator of Weiwu circuit affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Bao Xiurang sent Li Ruyin's head to Qiantang. King Hong Zong of Wuyue put Chief Minister Wu Cheng of Shanyin in charge of Weiwu.

sentences.zh: 吳越王弘倧，性剛嚴，憤忠獻王弘佐時容養諸將，政非己出，及襲位，誅杭、越侮法吏三人。

translations.literal: Wuyue King Hong Zong was by nature stern and severe; he resented that under Loyal and Offering King Hong Zuo the generals had been indulged and policy was not his own, and when he succeeded to the throne he executed three legal officers of Hang and Yue who had shown contempt for the law.
translations.idiomatic: King Hong Zong of Wuyue was stern and unyielding by nature. He resented that under his predecessor, Loyal and Offering King Hong Zuo, the generals had been indulged and he had held no real power. As soon as he took the throne he executed three legal officers from Hang and Yue who had flouted the law.

sentences.zh: 內牙統軍使胡進思恃迎立功，干預政事；

translations.literal: Inner Guards commander Hu Jinsi relied on his merit in welcoming the succession and interfered in government affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Hu Jinsi, commander of the Inner Guards, counted on his role in bringing Hong Zong to the throne and meddled constantly in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 弘倧惡之，欲授以一州，進思不可。

translations.literal: Hong Zong hated this and wished to assign him a prefecture; Jinsi would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zong loathed this and tried to send him off to govern a prefecture, but Jinsi refused to go.

sentences.zh: 進思有所謀議，弘倧數面折之。

translations.literal: Whenever Jinsi had some plan or proposal, Hong Zong repeatedly rebuked him to his face.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Jinsi offered advice, Hong Zong contradicted him openly and to his face.

sentences.zh: 進思還家，設忠獻王位，被髮慟哭。

translations.literal: Jinsi returned home, set up Loyal and Offering King's spirit tablet, let down his hair, and wept in anguish.
translations.idiomatic: Jinsi went home, set up a spirit tablet for Loyal and Offering King, loosened his hair, and wept in grief.

sentences.zh: 民有殺牛者，吏按之，引人所市肉近千斤。

translations.literal: A commoner had killed an ox; the clerk investigated and led in the man, whose meat sold at market came to nearly a thousand jin.
translations.idiomatic: A man was accused of slaughtering an ox. The investigating clerk produced nearly a thousand jin of meat the man had sold.

sentences.zh: 弘倧問進思：「牛大者肉幾何？」

translations.literal: Hong Zong asked Jinsi, "How much meat does a large ox yield?"
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zong asked Jinsi, "How much meat does a large ox yield?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「不過三百斤。」

translations.literal: He replied, "No more than three hundred jin."
translations.idiomatic: Jinsi answered, "No more than three hundred jin.

sentences.zh: 弘倧曰：「然則吏妄也。」

translations.literal: Hong Zong said, "Then the clerk has lied."
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zong said, "Then the clerk is lying.

sentences.zh: 命按其罪。

translations.literal: He ordered the crime investigated against him.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the clerk punished.

sentences.zh: 進思拜賀其明。

translations.literal: Jinsi bowed and congratulated him on his clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Jinsi bowed and praised his discernment.

sentences.zh: 弘人宗曰：「公何能知其詳？」

translations.literal: Hong Renzong said, "How can you know such details?"
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zong said, "How do you know that so precisely?

sentences.zh: 進思踧躇對曰：「臣昔未從軍，亦嘗從事於此。」

translations.literal: Jinsi, flustered, replied, "Your subject in former days before entering the army also once worked at this trade."
translations.idiomatic: Jinsi hesitated and said, "Before I took up arms, Your Majesty, I worked at that trade myself.

sentences.zh: 進思以弘倧為知其素業，故辱之，益恨怒。

translations.literal: Jinsi thought Hong Zong knew his former occupation and so had shamed him; his hatred and anger grew.
translations.idiomatic: Jinsi believed Hong Zong had exposed his humble past on purpose. His resentment deepened.

sentences.zh: 進思建議遣李孺贇歸福州，及孺贇叛，弘倧責之，進思愈不自安。

translations.literal: Jinsi had advised sending Li Ruyin back to Fuzhou; when Ruyin rebelled, Hong Zong blamed him, and Jinsi grew ever more ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Jinsi had urged sending Li Ruyin back to Fuzhou. When Ruyin rebelled, Hong Zong blamed Jinsi, who grew only more uneasy.

sentences.zh: 弘倧與內牙指揮使何承訓謀逐進思，又謀於內都監使水丘昭券，昭券以為進思黨盛難制，不如容之，弘倧猶豫未決。

translations.literal: Hong Zong with Inner Guards director He Chengxun plotted to drive Jinsi out; he also consulted Inner Palace Directorate commissioner Shuiqiu Zhaoquan, who said Jinsi's faction was strong and hard to control, better to tolerate him—Hong Zong hesitated and did not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zong and Inner Guards director He Chengxun plotted to expel Jinsi. Hong Zong also consulted Inner Palace Directorate commissioner Shuiqiu Zhaoquan, who argued that Jinsi's faction was too strong to confront and that it would be wiser to tolerate him. Hong Zong wavered and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 承訓恐事洩，反以謀告進思。

translations.literal: Chengxun feared the affair would leak and instead told the plot to Jinsi.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun, fearing exposure, betrayed the plot to Jinsi instead.

sentences.zh: 庚戌晦，弘倧夜宴將吏，進思疑其圖己，與其黨謀作亂，帥親兵百人戎服執兵入見於天策堂，曰：「老奴無罪，王何故圖之？」

translations.literal: On the last day of gengxu, Hong Zong held a night banquet for officers; Jinsi suspected he was plotting against him, conspired with his faction to raise a disturbance, and led a hundred personal troops in armor bearing arms to an audience in the Celestial Strategy Hall, saying, "This old slave is guiltless—why does the King plot against me?"
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of gengxu Hong Zong gave a night banquet for his officers. Jinsi suspected a trap and conspired with his followers to strike first. He led a hundred armored retainers into the Celestial Strategy Hall and demanded, "This old servant has done no wrong. Why does Your Majesty plot against me?

sentences.zh: 弘倧叱之不退，左右持兵者皆憤怒。

translations.literal: Hong Zong shouted at him but he would not withdraw; those on left and right holding weapons were all enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zong shouted at him, but Jinsi would not leave. The armed attendants on both sides seethed with anger.

sentences.zh: 弘倧猝愕不暇發言，趨入義和院。

translations.literal: Hong Zong, suddenly startled, had no time to speak and hurried into the Yihe Courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Caught off guard, Hong Zong had no chance to reply and fled into the Yihe Courtyard.

sentences.zh: 進思鎖其門，矯稱王命，告中外云：「猝得風疾，傳位於同參相府事弘俶。」

translations.literal: Jinsi locked the door, falsely claimed the King's command, and announced within and without, "He has suddenly taken a wind ailment and transfers the throne to Hong Chu, who shares in administering the chief minister's office."
translations.idiomatic: Jinsi locked the door behind him, forged a royal decree, and announced to the court and the realm, "The King has been stricken with a sudden palsy and transfers the throne to Hong Chu, who already shares in governing.

sentences.zh: 進思因帥諸將迎弘俶於私第，且召丞相元德昭。

translations.literal: Jinsi then led the generals to welcome Hong Chu at his private residence, and also summoned chief minister Yuan Dezhao.
translations.idiomatic: Jinsi then led the generals to Hong Chu's private residence to install him and summoned Chief Minister Yuan Dezhao.

sentences.zh: 德昭至，立於簾外不拜，曰：「俟見新君。」

translations.literal: Dezhao arrived, stood outside the curtain and did not bow, saying, "I await seeing the new ruler."
translations.idiomatic: Dezhao came but stood outside the curtain without bowing. "I will bow," he said, "when I have seen the new ruler.

sentences.zh: 進思亟出褰簾，德昭乃拜。

translations.literal: Jinsi hastily came out and lifted the curtain; only then did Dezhao bow.
translations.idiomatic: Jinsi hurried out and drew back the curtain. Only then did Dezhao bow.

sentences.zh: 進思稱弘倧之命，承製授弘俶鎮海、鎮東節度使兼侍中。

translations.literal: Jinsi claimed Hong Zong's command and, receiving the edict, invested Hong Chu as military governor of Zhenhai and Zhendong and concurrently Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Hong Zong's name Jinsi issued an edict appointing Hong Chu military governor of Zhenhai and Zhendong and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 弘俶曰：「能全吾兄，乃敢承命。

translations.literal: Hong Chu said, "Only if you can preserve my elder brother entirely do I dare accept the command.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Chu said, "I will accept only if my brother is kept safe.

sentences.zh: 不然，當避賢路。」

translations.literal: Otherwise I should yield the path to the worthy."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I must step aside for someone worthier.

sentences.zh: 進思許之。

translations.literal: Jinsi promised him.
translations.idiomatic: Jinsi agreed.

sentences.zh: 弘俶始視事。

translations.literal: Hong Chu then began to conduct affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Hong Chu then took up the duties of rule."

sentences.zh: 進思殺水丘昭券及進侍鄜光鉉。

translations.literal: Jinsi killed Shuiqiu Zhaoquan and advancing attendant Fu Guangxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jinsi killed Shuiqiu Zhaoquan and palace attendant Fu Guangxuan.

sentences.zh: 光鉉，弘倧之舅也。

translations.literal: Guangxuan was Hong Zong's maternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxuan was Hong Zong's uncle on his mother's side.

sentences.zh: 進思之妻曰：「它人猶可殺，昭券，君子也，奈何害之！」

translations.literal: Jinsi's wife said, "Others may still be killed, but Zhaoquan is a gentleman—how can you harm him!"
translations.idiomatic: Jinsi's wife protested, "Others you might kill, but Zhaoquan is a man of honor. How can you harm him?"

sentences.zh: 是歲，唐主以羽林大將軍王延政為安化節度使、鄱陽王，鎮饒州。

translations.literal: That year, the Tang ruler made Imperial Guard general Wang Yanzheng Anhua military governor and Prince of Poyang, garrisoning Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Tang emperor made Wang Yanzheng, a general of the Imperial Guard, military governor of Anhua and Prince of Poyang, with his seat at Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖睿文聖武昭肅孝皇帝中乾祐元年（

translations.literal: Mid-reign of Gaozu Emperor, styled Ruiwen Shengwu Zhaosu Xiaohuangdi, first year of Qianyou (
translations.idiomatic: Mid-reign of Emperor Gaozu, posthumously styled Ruiwen Shengwu Zhaosu Xiaohuangdi, first year of Qianyou (

sentences.zh: 戊申，公元九四八年）

translations.literal: wushen, corresponding to the year 948 CE)
translations.idiomatic: wushen, corresponding to 948 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙卯，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on yimao, great amnesty and change of era name.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on yimao, the court proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the reign title.

sentences.zh: 帝以趙匡贊、侯益與蜀兵共為寇，患之。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Zhao Kuangzan and Hou Yi together with Shu troops were raiding as enemies, was troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was troubled that Zhao Kuangzan and Hou Yi were raiding alongside Shu troops.

sentences.zh: 會回鶻入貢，訴稱為党項所阻，乞兵應接。

translations.literal: It happened that the Uyghurs came to offer tribute, complaining they had been blocked by the Tangut, and begged troops to meet and escort them.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Uyghur envoys arrived with tribute, complaining that Tangut forces had blocked their way and asking for troops to escort them through.

sentences.zh: 詔右衛大將軍王景崇、將軍齊藏珍將禁軍數千赴之，因使之經略關西。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Right Guard general Wang Jingchong and general Qi Canzhen to lead several thousand palace troops to go to them, and thereby had them take charge of Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Right Guard general Wang Jingchong and general Qi Canzhen to march several thousand palace troops to their aid and, in doing so, to take charge of operations in Guanxi.

sentences.zh: 晉昌節度判官李恕，久在趙延壽幕下，延壽使之佐匡贊。

translations.literal: Jinchang circuit aide Li Shu had long been in Zhao Yanshou's staff; Yanshou had him assist Kuangzan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shu, aide to the Jinchang military governor, had long served on Zhao Yanshou's staff. Yanshou sent him to advise Kuangzan.

sentences.zh: 匡贊將入蜀，恕諫曰：「燕王入胡，豈所願哉！

translations.literal: Kuangzan was about to enter Shu; Li Shu remonstrated, saying, "The Prince of Yan entered the barbarians' land—was that his wish!
translations.idiomatic: When Kuangzan prepared to throw in his lot with Shu, Li Shu urged him, "Did the Prince of Yan go into captivity among the Khitan because he wanted to?

sentences.zh: 今漢家新得天下，方務招懷，若謝罪歸朝，必保富貴。

translations.literal: Now the House of Han has newly gained the realm and is bent on winning men over; if you confess guilt and return to court, you are sure to be kept in wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: The Han court has only just won the realm and is eager to win men over. If you confess your fault and return to court, you are sure to keep your rank and fortune.

sentences.zh: 入蜀非全計也，『蹄涔不容尺鯉』，公必悔之。」

translations.literal: Entering Shu is not a plan for safety; 'a hoof-print puddle cannot hold a foot-long carp'—you will surely regret it."
translations.idiomatic: Shu is no safe harbor. As the saying goes, 'A hoof-print puddle cannot hold a foot-long carp.' You will regret this.

sentences.zh: 匡贊乃遣恕奉表請入朝。

translations.literal: Kuangzan then sent Shu to present a memorial requesting entry at court.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangzan then sent Li Shu with a memorial asking permission to come to court.

sentences.zh: 景崇等未行而恕至，帝問恕：「匡贊何為附蜀？」

translations.literal: Jingchong and the others had not yet set out when Shu arrived; the Emperor asked Shu, "Why did Kuangzan attach himself to Shu?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingchong's column had not yet marched when Li Shu arrived. The Emperor asked him, "Why did Kuangzan side with Shu?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「匡贊自以身受虜官，父在虜庭，恐陛下未之察，故附蜀求苟免耳。

translations.literal: He replied, "Kuangzan himself, because he had accepted an office under the barbarians and his father was in the barbarian court, feared Your Majesty had not yet perceived this, and so attached himself to Shu seeking a bare escape.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shu answered, "Kuangzan accepted office under the Khitan, and his father remains in their court. He feared Your Majesty had not yet understood his position, so he turned to Shu only to save his skin.

sentences.zh: 臣以為國家必應存撫，故遣臣來祈哀。」

translations.literal: Your subject thought the state surely ought to preserve and comfort him, and so sent your subject to plead for mercy."
translations.idiomatic: He believes the court will surely show mercy, and that is why he sent me to beg for forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「匡贊父子，本吾人也，不幸陷虜。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Father and son Kuangzan are originally our own people, who unhappily fell among the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Father and son Kuangzan are our own people who were unfortunate enough to fall into Khitan hands.

sentences.zh: 今延壽方墜檻阱，吾何忍更害匡贊乎！」

translations.literal: Now Yanshou has just fallen into a cage-trap—how could I bear to harm Kuangzan further!"
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou has only just fallen into the Khitan's trap. How could I bear to harm Kuangzan as well!

sentences.zh: 即聽其入朝。

translations.literal: He immediately permitted him to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: He at once allowed him to come to court.

sentences.zh: 侯益亦請赴二月四日聖壽節上壽。

translations.literal: Hou Yi also requested to go and offer birthday congratulations at the Holy Longevity Festival on the fourth day of the second month.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Yi also asked to attend court and offer birthday felicitations at the Holy Longevity Festival on the fourth day of the second month.

sentences.zh: 景崇等將行，帝召入臥內，敕之曰：「匡贊、益之心，皆未可知。

translations.literal: As Jingchong and the others were about to set out, the Emperor summoned them into his bedchamber and charged them, saying, "The minds of Kuangzan and Yi are both still unknown.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jingchong's column was about to march, the Emperor called them into his bedchamber and instructed them: "The intentions of Kuangzan and Hou Yi are still uncertain.

sentences.zh: 汝至彼，彼已入朝，則勿問；

translations.literal: When you reach there, if they have already entered court, then do not question them;
translations.idiomatic: When you arrive, if they have already come to court, leave them be;

sentences.zh: 若尚遷延顧望，當以便宜從事。」

translations.literal: if they still delay and look about, you should act according to what the occasion requires."
translations.idiomatic: if they still linger and waver, act as the situation demands."

sentences.zh: 己未，帝更名暠。

translations.literal: On jiwei, the Emperor changed his name to Gao.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, the Emperor changed his name to Gao.

sentences.zh: 以前威勝節度使馮道為太師。

translations.literal: He appointed former Weisheng military governor Feng Dao as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Feng Dao, former military governor of Weisheng, Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，吳越王弘俶遷故王弘倧於衣錦軍私第，遣匡武都頭薛溫將親兵衛之。

translations.literal: On renxu, King Hongchu of Wuyue moved the former king Hongzuan to a private residence in the Yijin Army cantonment and sent Kuangwu company head Xue Wen to lead personal troops to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, King Hongchu of Wuyue moved the deposed king Hongzuan to a private residence at the Yijin garrison and dispatched Xue Wen, head of the Kuangwu company, with household troops to guard him.

sentences.zh: 潛戒之曰：「若有非常處分，皆非吾意，當以死拒之。」

translations.literal: He secretly warned him, saying, "If there is any extraordinary disposition, none of it is my intent—you should resist it unto death."
translations.idiomatic: He secretly warned Xue Wen: "If anyone tries to take extraordinary measures against him, that is not my wish. Resist with your life."

sentences.zh: 帝自魏王承訓卒，悲痛過甚。

translations.literal: Since the Prince of Wei's Chengyun's death, the Emperor's grief had been excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since the death of Prince of Wei Chengyun, the Emperor had grieved beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 甲子，始不豫。

translations.literal: On jiazi, he first fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, he fell gravely ill for the first time.

sentences.zh: 趙匡贊不俟李恕返命，已離長安。

translations.literal: Zhao Kuangzan did not wait for Li Shu to return with his reply and had already left Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kuangzan did not wait for Li Shu to return with the Emperor's answer and had already left Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 丙子，入見。

translations.literal: On bingzi, he entered and was received in audience.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, he entered the capital and had audience with the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 王景崇等至長安，聞蜀兵已入秦川，以兵少，發本道及趙匡贊牙兵千餘人同拒之。

translations.literal: Wang Jingchong and the others reached Chang'an; hearing that Shu troops had already entered Qinchuan, because their forces were few they raised more than a thousand local troops and Zhao Kuangzan's personal soldiers to resist together.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingchong reached Chang'an and learned that Shu forces had already entered Qinchuan. His troops were too few, so he raised more than a thousand men from his own circuit and Zhao Kuangzan's household guard to resist them.

sentences.zh: 景崇恐匡贊牙兵亡逸，欲文其面，微露風旨。

translations.literal: Jingchong feared Kuangzan's personal soldiers would flee and scatter, wished to tattoo their faces, and lightly let slip his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchong feared Zhao Kuangzan's men would desert and wanted to tattoo their faces, hinting at his intention.

sentences.zh: 軍校趙思綰，首請自文其面以帥下，景崇悅。

translations.literal: Army officer Zhao Sinian was the first to request that he tattoo his own face to lead the men below; Jingchong was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: An army officer named Zhao Sinian was the first to offer to tattoo his own face to set an example for the men. Jingchong was pleased.

sentences.zh: 齊藏珍竊言曰：「思綰凶暴難制，不如殺之。」

translations.literal: Qi Canzhen whispered, saying, "Sinian is fierce and brutal and hard to control—better to kill him."
translations.idiomatic: Qi Canzhen said privately, "Sinian is brutal and impossible to control. Better kill him now.

sentences.zh: 景崇不聽。

translations.literal: Jingchong would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchong refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 思綰，魏州人也。

translations.literal: Sinian was a man of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sinian was from Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 蜀李廷珪將至長安，聞趙匡贊已入朝，欲引歸，王景崇邀之，敗廷珪於子午谷。

translations.literal: Li Tinggui of Shu was about to reach Chang'an; hearing Zhao Kuangzan had already entered court, he wished to lead his force back. Wang Jingchong intercepted him and defeated Tinggui at Ziwu Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tinggui of Shu was marching on Chang'an. When he learned Zhao Kuangzan had already surrendered to the Han court, he turned to withdraw. Wang Jingchong intercepted him and defeated his force at Ziwu Valley.

sentences.zh: 張虔釗至寶雞，諸將議不協，按兵未進。

translations.literal: Zhang Qianzhao reached Baoji; the generals' counsel was not united and they held their troops without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qianzhao reached Baoji, but the generals could not agree on a plan and held their troops without advancing.

sentences.zh: 侯益聞廷珪西還，因閉壁拒蜀兵，虔釗勢孤，引兵夜遁。

translations.literal: Hou Yi heard Tinggui had returned west and therefore shut his walls and refused the Shu troops. Qianzhao was isolated in strength and led his army in flight by night.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Yi heard Tinggui was retreating west and shut his defenses against the Shu army. Isolated and outmatched, Qianzhao fled by night with his troops.

sentences.zh: 景崇帥鳳翔、隴、邠、涇、鄜、坊之兵追敗蜀兵於散關，俘將卒四百人。

translations.literal: Jingchong led troops from Fengxiang, Long, Bin, Jing, Fu, and Fang in pursuit and defeated Shu troops at Sanguan, capturing more than four hundred officers and men.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchong led forces from Fengxiang, Long, Bin, Jing, Fu, and Fang in pursuit and routed the Shu army at Sanguan Pass, taking more than four hundred officers and men prisoner.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，帝大漸，楊邠忌侍衛馬軍都指揮使、忠武節度使劉信，立遣之鎮。

translations.literal: On dingchou, the Emperor was critically ill. Yang Bin resented the Palace Horse Corps commander, Zhongwu military governor Liu Xin, and immediately sent him to his post.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, the Emperor lay near death. Yang Bin envied the commander of the palace horse corps and Zhongwu military governor Liu Xin and at once sent him back to his post.

sentences.zh: 信不得奉辭，雨泣而去。

translations.literal: Xin could not take leave in audience and departed weeping as in rain.
translations.idiomatic: Xin could not even bid the Emperor farewell and left in tears.

sentences.zh: 帝召蘇逢吉、楊邠、史弘肇、郭威入受顧命，曰：「餘氣息微，不能多言。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Su Fengji, Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao, and Guo Wei to receive his final charge and said, "My remaining breath is faint; I cannot speak much.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned Su Fengji, Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao, and Guo Wei to receive his deathbed instructions. He said, "My breath grows faint. I cannot say much.

sentences.zh: 承祐幼弱，後事托在卿輩。」

translations.literal: Chengyou is young and weak; the affairs that follow are entrusted to you gentlemen."
translations.idiomatic: Chengyou is still a boy. I leave what comes next to you.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「善防重威。」

translations.literal: He also said, "Take good care to guard against Chongwei."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Guard carefully against Chongwei.

sentences.zh: 是日，殂於萬歲殿，逢吉等秘不發喪。

translations.literal: That day he died in the Hall of Myriad Years; Fengji and the others kept the death secret and did not announce mourning.
translations.idiomatic: That day he died in the Hall of Myriad Years. Fengji and the others kept his death secret and did not announce mourning.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，下詔，稱：「重威父子，因朕小疾，謗議搖眾，並其子弘璋、弘璉、弘璨皆斬之。

translations.literal: On gengchen, an edict was issued stating, "Father and son Chongwei, taking advantage of our slight illness, slandered and stirred the multitude—we have beheaded them together with his sons Hongzhang, Honglian, and Hongcan.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, an edict was issued: "Du Chongwei and his sons, exploiting Our slight illness, spread slander and stirred unrest. Chongwei and his sons Hongzhang, Honglian, and Hongcan are all to be executed.

sentences.zh: 晉公主及內外親族，一切不問。」

translations.literal: The Princess of Jin and all kin inside and outside are not to be questioned in any matter."
translations.idiomatic: The Jin princess and all other relatives—inside or outside the family—are not to be prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 磔重威屍於市，市人爭啖其肉，吏不能禁，斯須而盡。

translations.literal: Chongwei's corpse was dismembered and exposed in the market; market people vied to eat his flesh, and officials could not forbid it—in a moment it was gone."
translations.idiomatic: Chongwei's corpse was dismembered and exposed in the market. Crowds fought over his flesh, and the officials could not stop them. In moments nothing remained."

sentences.zh: 二月，辛巳朔，立皇子左衛大將軍、大內都點檢承祐為周王，同平章事。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the first day xinsi, the prince, Left Guard general and Grand Inner Palace inspector Chengyou, was established as Prince of Zhou and made Tong Pingzhangshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the first day (xinsi), the Emperor's son Chengyou—Left Guard general and chief inspector of the inner palace—was named Prince of Zhou and appointed co-director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 有頃，發喪，宣遺制，令周王即皇帝位。

translations.literal: Before long mourning was announced and the testamentary decree proclaimed, ordering the Prince of Zhou to take the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward mourning was announced and the testamentary decree proclaimed, naming the Prince of Zhou emperor.

sentences.zh: 時年十八。

translations.literal: He was then eighteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was eighteen years old.

sentences.zh: 蜀韓保貞、龐福誠引兵自隴州還，要何重建俱西。

translations.literal: Han Baozhen and Pang Fucheng of Shu led troops back from Longzhou to intercept He Chongjian and go west together.
translations.idiomatic: Han Baozhen and Pang Fucheng of Shu led their troops back from Longzhou, intending to take He Chongjian west with them.

sentences.zh: 是日，保貞等至秦州，分兵守諸門及衢路，重建遂入於蜀。

translations.literal: That day Baozhen and the others reached Qinzhou, divided their troops to guard all gates and thoroughfares, and Chongjian then entered Shu.
translations.idiomatic: That day they reached Qinzhou, posted troops at every gate and main road, and He Chongjian fled into Shu.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，尊皇后曰皇太后。

translations.literal: On dinghai, the empress was honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, the empress was honored as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 朝廷知成德留後白再榮非將帥才，庚寅，以前建雄留後劉在明代之。

translations.literal: The court knew that Chengde acting military governor Bai Zairong was not a general's talent; on gengyin the former Jianxiong acting military governor Liu Zaiming was appointed to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: The court knew Bai Zairong, acting military governor of Chengde, lacked the talent of a commander. On gengyin Liu Zaiming, former acting governor of Jianxiong, replaced him.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，大赦。

translations.literal: On guisi, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 吳越內牙指揮使何承訓復請誅胡進思及其黨。

translations.literal: He Chengxun, Wuyue inner-palace commandant, again requested the execution of Hu Jinsi and his faction.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengxun, the Wuyue inner-palace commander, again asked that Hu Jinsi and his faction be put to death.

sentences.zh: 吳越王弘俶惡其反覆，且懼召禍，乙未，執承訓，斬之。

translations.literal: King Hongchu of Wuyue hated his vacillation and also feared he would invite disaster; on yiwei he seized Chengxun and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: King Hongchu despised his vacillation and feared he would bring disaster on them. On yiwei he arrested Chengxun and executed him.

sentences.zh: 進思屢請殺廢王弘倧以絕後患，弘俶不許。

translations.literal: Jinsi repeatedly requested killing the deposed king Hongzuan to cut off later troubles; Hongchu would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Jinsi repeatedly urged that the deposed king Hongzuan be killed to remove a future threat. Hongchu refused.

sentences.zh: 進思詐以王命密令薛溫害之。

translations.literal: Jinsi falsely used the king's command secretly to order Xue Wen to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Jinsi forged a royal order and secretly told Xue Wen to kill Hongzuan.

sentences.zh: 溫曰：「僕受命之日，不聞此言，不敢妄發。」

translations.literal: Wen said, "On the day I received my commission I did not hear these words, and I dare not act rashly."
translations.idiomatic: Xue Wen said, "When I took this commission I heard nothing of this. I dare not act on my own.

sentences.zh: 進思乃夜遣其黨方安等二人□俞垣而入，弘倧闔戶拒之，大呼求救；

translations.literal: Jinsi then by night sent two of his partisans, Fang An and another, □ over the wall to enter; Hongzuan shut the door and refused them and cried out for help;
translations.idiomatic: That night Jinsi sent two followers, Fang An and another, to climb over the wall. Hongzuan barred the door and shouted for help;

sentences.zh: 溫聞之，率眾而入，斃安等於庭中。

translations.literal: Wen heard this, led his troops inside, and killed An and the others in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Wen heard the uproar, led his men in, and killed Fang An and the others in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 入告弘俶，弘俶大驚，曰：「全吾兄，汝之力也。」

translations.literal: He entered and reported to Hongchu; Hongchu was greatly alarmed and said, "You have preserved my elder brother—the credit is yours."
translations.idiomatic: He reported to Hongchu, who was greatly shaken. "You have saved my brother," he said. "I owe you for this.

sentences.zh: 弘俶畏忌進思，曲意下之。

translations.literal: Hongchu feared and was wary of Jinsi and humored him with yielding intent.
translations.idiomatic: Hongchu feared Jinsi and treated him with studied deference.

sentences.zh: 進思亦內憂懼，未幾，疽發背卒。

translations.literal: Jinsi also inwardly worried and feared; before long a carbuncle broke out on his back and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Jinsi was inwardly uneasy as well. Before long a carbuncle broke out on his back and he died.

sentences.zh: 弘倧由是獲全。

translations.literal: Hongzuan thereby obtained safety.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzuan was thus spared.

sentences.zh: 詔以王景崇兼鳳翔巡檢使。

translations.literal: An edict made Wang Jingchong concurrently Fengxiang patrol commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingchong was ordered to serve concurrently as patrol commissioner of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 景崇引兵至鳳翔，侯益尚未行，景崇以禁兵分守諸門。

translations.literal: Jingchong led troops to Fengxiang; Hou Yi had not yet departed, and Jingchong used palace troops to guard all gates separately.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchong marched to Fengxiang. Hou Yi had not yet left, and Jingchong posted palace troops at every gate.

sentences.zh: 或勸景崇殺益，景崇以受先朝密旨，嗣主未之知，或疑於專殺，猶豫未決。

translations.literal: Someone urged Jingchong to kill Yi; Jingchong, because he had received a secret charge from the former court and the succeeding sovereign did not know of it, feared suspicion of unauthorized killing and hesitated without deciding.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to kill Hou Yi. Jingchong had received secret instructions from the late Emperor, but the new sovereign did not know of them. He feared being accused of murder on his own authority and hesitated.

sentences.zh: 益聞之，不告景崇而去，景崇悔，自詬。

translations.literal: Yi heard of this and departed without telling Jingchong; Jingchong regretted it and reviled himself.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Yi heard of the plot and slipped away without telling Jingchong. Jingchong regretted his hesitation and cursed himself.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，益入朝，隱帝問：「何故召蜀軍？」

translations.literal: On wuxu, Yi entered court; the Hidden Emperor asked, "Why did you summon Shu troops?"
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Hou Yi had audience with the Hidden Emperor, who asked, "Why did you invite the Shu army?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣欲誘致而殺之。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Your subject wished to lure them in and kill them."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I meant to lure them in and destroy them.

sentences.zh: 帝哂之。

translations.literal: The Emperor smiled at him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor gave a sceptical smile.

sentences.zh: 蜀張虔釗自恨無功。

translations.literal: Zhang Qianzhao of Shu blamed himself for having no achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qianzhao of Shu was bitter at his failure.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，至興州，慚忿而卒。

translations.literal: On guimao he reached Xingzhou and died of shame and anger.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao he reached Xingzhou and died there, consumed by shame and rage.

sentences.zh: 侍衛馬步都指揮使、同平章事史弘肇遭母喪，不數日，復出朝參。

translations.literal: Shi Hongzhao, Palace Horse and Foot Corps commander and Tong Pingzhangshi, met his mother's mourning; within not many days he again came out to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hongzhao, commander of the palace horse and foot corps and co-director of the Secretariat, lost his mother but returned to court within a few days.
